name: Justin J. Pearson
subject: The future of the Voting Rights Act depends on us
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Committee to Elect Justin J
body:
The Supreme Court has agreed to hear a case that could gut the landmark law.
| [ ](https://jj-p.org/l/iuXop2a0pDQZ?t=cWA2soqydOg2)
---
Peter,

The Supreme Court has agreed to hear _Louisiana v. Callais_ — a case that could further **gut one of the most powerful protections in our democracy: the Voting Rights Act of 1965.** [](https://jj-p.org/l/MMB4Q4yo4n3e) This law was written with the sacrifices of those who marched, bled, and even died to secure the right to vote for Black Americans and other marginalized communities.

Now, more than 60 years later, that right is back on trial and under _intense_ scrutiny.

That's why I'm asking you — from the heart — to stand up for our democracy right now, because power never concedes without pressure, and justice never wins without People showing up. [Please take a moment to add your name to our petition now to demand the Supreme Court protect the Voting Rights Act today.](https://jj-p.org/l/hJWrmDkRpYl2) | [Add Your Name »](https://jj-p.org/l/8e0EKNtQqKs7)
---
If the Court overturns Section 2 of the VRA, it will make it _nearly impossible_ to challenge blatantly racist gerrymandering and voter suppression — giving extremists the green light to redraw congressional maps that will silence Black, Brown, and Indigenous voters for generations.

**This _isn't_ about politics. It's about power. It's about whether our voices matter as much as the billionaires and politicians who want to rig our democracy to keep their seats, their donors, and their control.**

That's _not_ the America my ancestors fought for, and it's _not_ the future I believe in.

I believe in us — in our ability to resist despair, to choose faith, and to stand together for the pursuit of justice.

Every moment like this one reminds us that democracy doesn't defend itself — we the People must rise up and fight to protect it.

[So please — join our Movement's fight for a better tomorrow by adding your name to our petition to protect the Voting Rights Act.](https://jj-p.org/l/bOxvqauO186V)
[Add Your Name »](https://jj-p.org/l/6vMkOhaxmOf0)
---
In Love and Service,

Justin J. Pearson

| | I hope this email finds you well and ready to VOTE! We're gaining steam every day, and I'm thrilled to share how we're connecting with voters and building a strong campaign to take on Alma Adams. First off, our yard signs are hitting the streets! We're distributing signs throughout the district. If you haven't received yours yet, please reply to this email to request one. I've also been out meeting with business and community leaders who share our passion for revitalizing our economy and neighborhoods. From small business owners in Plaza Midwood to faith leaders in West Charlotte, the conversations have been inspiring. They're ready for change, lower taxes, less regulation, and more opportunities for our district. These partnerships are key to our vision of a prosperous NC-12! On top of that, I've been chatting with local media outlets to spread our positive message far and wide. Recent interviews with WBT Radio and the Charlotte Observer highlighted our plans to tackle affordability, community safety, support law enforcement, and empower our schools. The response has been fantastic, voters are tuning in and seeing why it's time for fresh leadership! Overall, friends, this campaign is on fire! With your support, we're proving that republican values can resonate here in the heart of Charlotte. We're not just running against the status quo; we're building a movement for real results like safer streets, better jobs, and a government that works for the people. Together, we're unstoppable! As a reminder, early voting kicks off on February 12th, that's just days away! Mark your calendars, grab your ID, and head to the polls to cast your vote for change. Every voice counts in making NC-12 stronger. Thank you for standing with me. Let's win this! In service,Addul Ali

** FRIDAY FOCUS
------------------------------------------------------------

January 30, 2026

Welcome to the Friday Focus: your end-of-week snapshot from Team Mai with updates, upcoming events, and ways to plug into our people powered campaign.

** NEWS & UPDATES
------------------------------------------------------------

Something incredible happened in New Jersey last night.

AIPAC poured millions into attack ads, brought in corporate donors from across the country, and did everything they could to take down a grassroots candidate.

They lost and now, the Working Families Party endorsed Analilia Mejia on the cusp of victory in NJ-11. (https://punchbowl.news/article/campaigns/mejia-nj-upset/?utm_source=Mai+Vang+for+Congress&utm_campaign=2f95712060-EMAIL_CAMPAIGN_2026_01_31_12_06_COPY_01&utm_medium=email&utm_term=0_-f6b7740e04-529763991)

The people-powered campaign they tried to destroy is now winning, and honestly, it has me feeling so hopeful about our campaign.

Because here's the truth: corporate PACs are coming for our race too.

Doris Matsui has taken their money for 20+ years. I don't. And that means they're going to do everything they can to protect their investment and stop our movement before it gets to Congress.

But New Jersey just proved something I've believed since day one: when ordinary people come together, we can defeat even the most well-funded political machines. That's exactly what we're building here – not a campaign funded by corporate interests, but a movement of teachers, nurses, and families who refuse to be silenced.

Please join our grassroots movement. Donate. Volunteer. We can make history like they’ve done in New Jersey. (http://www.maiforus.com/maildonate?utm_source=Mai+Vang+for+Congress&utm_campaign=2f95712060-EMAIL_CAMPAIGN_2026_01_31_12_06_COPY_01&utm_medium=email&utm_term=0_-f6b7740e04-529763991)

Sincerely,

Mai Vang

Sunrise Movement Endorses Mai Vang for Congress

We just earned another major endorsement from the Sunrise Movement—the youth-led climate organization backing bold progressive leaders across the country.

"While establishment politicians make empty promises about reform, Mai Vang is taking real action. And she's doing it without taking corporate PAC money, because our democracy shouldn't be for sale."

This is what people-powered looks like. No corporate PACs. No special interest money. Just a movement of working people ready to take back our democracy.

The appeals court rejected every basis behind the lower court’s
unprecedented decision to keep the records secret. The court held that
the police investigative file is a public record, that the “ongoing
investigation” rationale for hiding the records is now moot as the
investigation is over, and that the court incorrectly imposed a
blanket secrecy rule based on speculative school-security or
copycat-crime concerns. It also rejected the trial court’s
unilateral creation of policy-based exemptions not found in statute.
The court also ruled that federal copyright law does not override the
Public Records Act and does not justify wholesale suppression of
records. Limited redactions may apply, but complete secrecy –
including for the shooter’s writings – is unlawful.

Communications between the [Federal Election Commission’s] Office of Compliance and any state attorney general’s office or the U.S. Department of Justice, about any alleged irregularities in ActBlue's donor verification policies and procedures, donor irregularities, or potential donor fraudulent activity. According to an April 2025 congressional joint interim staff report [], “Fraud on ActBlue: How the Democrats’ Top Fundraising Platform Opens the Door for Illegal Election Contributions:” Internal documents ... show that ActBlue staff and executives fail to take the threat of fraud seriously. ActBlue employees regularly demonstrated an unfounded belief that bad actors were not seeking to fraudulently contribute to Democrat campaigns and causes. For example, ActBlue’s training guide for new fraud-prevention employees instructed them to “look for reasons to accept contributions,” rather than err on the side of flagging a suspicious donation. * Altogether, ActBlue’s internal documents and communications paint a damning picture: despite repeated instances of fraudulent donations to Democrat campaigns and causes from domestic and foreign sources, ActBlue is not demonstrating a serious effort to deter fraud on its platform. [Emphasis in original] At best, ActBlue’s conduct displays a profound disrespect for the principle that only Americans should decide American elections. At worst, it may violate the Federal Election Campaign Act of 1971 (FECA), which states that persons who “knowingly accept a contribution made by one person in the name of another person” may face criminal liability. There are legitimate, grave concerns that ActBlue has enabled illegal fundraising. By failing to prevent widespread straw-donor schemes and other tactics, it is likely that fraudulent and even foreign-sourced contributions have crept into Democrat campaign coffers. We are a national leader in election integrity and voting rights litigation, with a record of successful lawsuits [] enforcing constitutional redistricting standards and cleaning voter rolls nationwide. On September 18, McMiller was arrested on first-degree murder charges arising from a September 11 “smash-and-grab” robbery at a Michigan Avenue Louis Vuitton store in Chicago that left one person dead. We filed the lawsuit in the Circuit Court of Sangamon County, Illinois, County Department, Chancery Division after Pritzker’s office failed to adequately respond to a September 22, 2025, FOIA request for: All photographs, images, or visual media depicting Governor JB Pritzker and Kellen McMiller (or any individual identified as a participant in the peacekeeper program wearing a “peacekeeper” vest) taken during the Governor’s visits to Chicago on or around September 5, 2025, including but not limited to the event in Englewood focused on community violence intervention. Friend – something’s been on my mind, and I need to know where you stand on it.
Donald Trump and his allies claim they’re championing “meritocracy.” But that’s absurd.
You can’t lecture me about “merit” and then make Pete Hegseth your Secretary of Defense.
You can’t lecture me about “merit” and then make Robert F. Kennedy Jr. your Secretary of Health and Human Services.
You can’t preach about promoting a “meritocracy” while filling your Cabinet with the most unfit, unqualified people ever selected.
**Let’s be clear: I’m doing everything I can to hold the line against this dangerous administration, and I need to know if you’re as concerned as I am about the threats Trump’s Cabinet poses to our country. Please, let me know now:**

Friend, I want America to win – because I love this country.
I love it in the same way we love our families. Many families have a complicated story. I carry in my veins the brutal side of that. My daddy had to give up his bus seat while wearing his soldier’s uniform – but because we kept fighting for America, his son now sits in a _Senate_ seat.

[](http://e.americanactionnews.com/rd/9z2z2gklhebj84orc8s7bv82jjadtjkrghboctn6ov8_rp22sh2s8i6epr0c5jm0p30cjh2bs) Yesterday I shared the numbers. Today I want to share the stories. An institution that believed it was above accountability. **They were wrong. And we have the footage to prove it.** Here are five investigations from 2025 that changed the game:
* **1\. THE $100 BILLION FEDERAL CONTRACTING SCAM (October)**
* We exposed ATI Government Solutions exploiting the SBA's 8(a) minority contracting program -- outsourcing 80% of their work while pocketing over $100 million in no-bid contracts. This wasn't a one-off. It was a systemic scheme across multiple agencies.
* **THE RESULT:** SBA suspension. $253 million in contracts halted. A $9 billion Treasury Department audit. Seven additional companies suspended. And a 15-year review of 8(a) contracts across every federal agency.
* **2\. GAO DATA THEFT CONFESSION (November)**
* A GAO director admitted on hidden camera that staff "stole and backed up" vaccine data specifically to block RFK Jr.'s HHS reforms. They weren't just resisting policy -- they were breaking federal law.
* **THE RESULT:** The director's profile was scrubbed. A federal investigation was launched. And the nation finally saw what "deep state resistance" actually looks like.
* **3\. NIH PORTRAIT DESTRUCTION (December)**
* NIH contractor Joseph Olmert confessed on camera to destroying official portraits of President Trump, Vice President Vance, RFK Jr., and Dr. Jay Bhattacharya. That's a potential 10-year federal felony -- destruction of government property.
* **THE RESULT:** Contractor FIRED. NIH internal investigation launched. And a national conversation about the defiance embedded in our federal agencies.
* **4\. GEORGETOWN PROFESSOR EXPOSED (December)**
* We caught a Georgetown professor on hidden camera calling Black conservatives "coons" and mocking "stupid white people." When we confronted him, he tried to assault our cameraman. Police were called.
* **THE RESULT:** Georgetown wiped his bio from their website. The footage went viral -- over 2 million views. And elite academic bias was laid bare for all to see.
* **5\. INSIDE EPSTEIN 'S ISLAND (May-December)**
* We released the first-ever footage from inside Jeffrey Epstein's private island mansion. We confronted a DOJ Deputy Chief who admitted plans to redact Republicans from the Epstein files. We published unredacted photos that Democrats tried to hide.
* **THE RESULT:** DOJ was forced to respond. Media outlets issued corrections. Joe Rogan covered our findings. And the truth about elite corruption reached millions who had been kept in the dark.

Dear Hoosier Republicans,

Growth and Accountability

Dear Hoosier Republicans,

2025 saw Indiana’s economy boom, outpacing our neighbors and the national trend at record-breaking speed. Wages increase by 10% year over year. The average wage of a new job jumped to more than $40 an hour. Job creators committed to hiring nearly 11,000 new employees. The cost to incentivize new jobs declined by 68%. These are the measurable results that dedicated conservative leadership has delivered.

At the same time, Governor Braun and our Republican leaders worked to restore accountability to state government. They achieved $465 million in Medicaid savings, stopped nearly $80 million in tax return fraud, identified more than 10,000 stolen identities, and eliminated 2,000 vacant positions.

This week’s announcements show that momentum isn't slowing, with new private-sector investment continuing to bring high-paying jobs to Indiana and decisive action to root out waste, fraud, and abuse across state government. Make no mistake, growth and accountability are on the ballot in November, and as today marks the last day to file for candidacy in 2026, that is what we will keep fighting for.

As always, thank you for being a part of our team, and please feel free to reach out if there's any way I can be of assistance.

Yours in service,

Lana Keesling, Indiana GOP Chairwoman

Governor Braun Fights Waste, Fraud, and Abuse in Government

Building on massive savings in 2025, Governor Braun signed Executive Order 26-04, creating the Indiana Council on Fraud Detection and Prevention to strengthen efforts to eliminate waste, fraud, and abuse in state government and protect taxpayer dollars.

"Hoosiers deserve honesty, transparency, and accountability in state government spending, and my administration is leading the nation in fighting financial fraud and improper payments, cutting costs, and enhancing transparency and accountability for Hoosier taxpayers."

- Governor Braun via a press release [https://events.in.gov/event/gov-braun-completes-seventh-annual-tour-of-all-92-counties]

Governor Braun Announces Kentucky Manufacturer, Recycler Relocating Headquarters to Indiana

Governor Braun announced that Global Polymers will relocate its headquarters and expand operations to Charlestown Indiana, investing more than $8.5 million in the state. The expansion will bring higher-than-average wages and strengthen Indiana’s recycling and manufacturing sector.

"By supporting Indiana companies and the Main Street economy, we’re helping businesses to grow, encouraging more high-wage career opportunities, and creating the next generation of entrepreneurs. All in all, these results will deliver a more robust economy."

- Governor Braun via a press release [https://events.in.gov/event/governor-braun-delivers-on-economic-development-strategy-increasing-opportunity-for-hoosiers-while-maximizing-taxpayer-dollars]

Indiana GOP is Hiring Interns for the Spring Semester

📱 News You Can Use

Governor Mike Braun ordered [https://events.in.gov/event/gov-mike-braun-orders-flags-lowered-to-half-staff-in-honor-of-former-us-representative-lee-hamilton] flags across Indiana to be lowered to half-staff in honor of former U.S. Representative Lee Hamilton, citing his lifetime of service and integrity. Flags will remain lowered statewide until sunset on the day of Hamilton’s interment.

Lieutenant Governor Micah Beckwith invited [https://events.in.gov/event/lt-governor-beckwith-invites-schools-to-apply-for-2026-lt-governors-stem-education-scholarship?utm_campaign=widget&utm_medium=widget&utm_source=State+of+Indiana] Indiana schools to apply for the 2026 Lt. Governors’ STEM Education Scholarship, which will award up to $1,000 to selected schools to support STEM programs and activities. Applications are open through March 6, 2026, with recipients announced in Spring 2026.

Secretary Diego Morales attended [https://events.in.gov/event/secretary-of-state-diego-morales-attends-2026-winter-nass-conference-meets-with-indiana-national-guard-and-us-senator-jim-banks?utm_campaign=widget&utm_medium=widget&utm_source=State+of+Indiana] the 2026 NASS Winter Conference in Washington, D.C., where he met with Indiana National Guard members and discussed improving voting access for deployed service members. Morales also met with Jim Banks to discuss election integrity initiatives.

Treasurer Daniel Elliott joined [https://x.com/DanielElliottIN/status/2019442546221502968] city and town leaders from across Indiana at the Annual Indiana Association of Counties Legislative Conference. Elliott emphasized that strong local government is key to a strong Hoosier economy and thanked local leaders for their service to their communities.

Attorney General Todd Rokita spoke [https://x.com/AGToddRokita/status/2019212222388707460] at the Association of Indiana Counties Legislative Conference and hosted an open house, connecting with county officials from across the state. Rokita emphasized shared priorities of trust, accountability, fiscal responsibility, and strong public safety collaboration to better serve Hoosiers.

State Comptroller Elise Nieshalla released [https://www.in.gov/comptroller/files/2025-State-of-Indianas-Financial-Report_RELEASE.pdf] Indiana’s 2025 State Financial Report, highlighting strong fiscal health with a $676 million surplus, $2.5 billion in reserves, and a reaffirmed AAA credit rating. Nieshalla emphasized Indiana’s continued fiscal discipline, noting the state’s low debt per capita, balanced budget, and expanded transparency efforts for Hoosiers.

Senator Todd Young applauded [https://www.young.senate.gov/newsroom/press-releases/young-applauds-senate-confirmation-of-justin-olson-for-southern-district-of-indiana/] the Senate confirmation of Justin Olson as a U.S. District Judge for the Southern District of Indiana, praising his integrity, legal excellence, and respect for the rule of law. Young highlighted Olson’s strong record of public service and said he looks forward to his service on the federal bench, serving Hoosiers across the district.

Senator Jim Banks urged Senate action on two priorities, calling [https://www.banks.senate.gov/news/press-releases/senator-banks-calls-for-passage-of-save-america-act/] for passage of the SAVE America Act to strengthen election security through proof-of-citizenship and voter ID requirements. Banks also pressed [https://www.banks.senate.gov/news/press-releases/senator-banks-urges-senate-passage-of-tylers-law/] for final passage of Tyler’s Law, a bipartisan bill aimed at improving fentanyl testing in emergency rooms to help prevent overdose deaths and save lives.

Congressman Rudy Yakym announced [https://yakym.house.gov/posts/yakym-announces-february-2026-staff-mobile-office-hours] February 2026 mobile staff office hours across Indiana’s Second District to assist constituents with federal casework. The one-on-one meetings provide residents an opportunity to connect directly with Yakym’s team for support and services.

### District 46,
**We are firmly in the second half of the 2026 Legislative Session, and it will be over before we know it.**

There are still so many critical bills moving through our statehouse, and so many opportunities to advance meaningful legislation actually aimed at improving the lives of Hoosiers and addressing the affordability crisis head-on.

As bills continue to move through the Senate and the House, we need you to keep showing up to speak on the bills that will impact you, your loved ones and your community.

**Thank you so much for your continued advocacy and your commitment to a better Indiana. **
**⬇️ Click to Find Out Three Tips I Wish I Knew About Testifying in Committee⬇️**
---
| [ ](https://click.subscription.in.gov/?%3D)
---
* * *
---
# **Important Update on SB 76**
---
| [ ](https://click.subscription.in.gov/?%3D)
---
### I have heard a lot of concern from our community about [SB 76](https://click.subscription.in.gov/?%3D "SB 76"), and I share it with you.

This bill, which passed out of the Senate before our deadline, would require all of our state's law enforcement to align itself with federal immigration enforcement.

By doing so, we are not sending a message that we are dedicated to law and order--in fact, just the opposite.

We cannot align ourselves with chaos, and I have been so proud of our community's refusal to do so.

This bill is moving in the House of Representatives, and is currently on the calendar for second reading--meaning it can be called for amendments before the entire body.

Keep calling, keep emailing, keep showing up.

Though it can feel like folks aren't listening or paying attention, we have seen over and over again that they are.
* * *
---
# **Taking a Moment to Recognize Hoosier Community Advocates**
---
| [ ](https://click.subscription.in.gov/?%3D)
---
### **I was honored to recognize Dr. Erica Graham, our 2026 Mrs. Indiana, for her tireless efforts to strengthen mental health support and elevate suicide prevention awareness for Hoosiers statewide.**
Dr. Graham is the founder of Shine Your Light, an education-based suicide prevention program designed to equip teachers, staff, students, parents and caregivers alike with the tools to recognize warning signs of suicidal ideation or mental health crises.

Her program teaches its participants to respond safely and compassionately and to connect at-risk individuals with appropriate professional help and ongoing support.

Indiana is stronger and healthier because of her leadership and compassion.

**Thank you, Dr. Graham, for your passion and advocacy. **

---
| [ ](https://click.subscription.in.gov/?%3D)
---
### I was so happy to take a few moments on our Senate floor to recognize National Girls & Women in Sports Day.

I'm proud to have authored SR 18, celebrating National Girls & Women in Sports Day and the strength, discipline and leadership that sports help build in every athlete.

I was grateful to have Miss Greater Indy 2026, Ginger Gordon, helping us honor this special occasion. Ginger founded a nonprofit, She's IN the Game, which focuses on empowering women and girls in the sports industry.

**Girls and women in sports don 't just change the game, they change the future! Strong, skilled and powerful.**
---

# **This Week in Committee**
---
|
---
### This Past Week, I served on three committees where we heard the following bills:

_Pensions and Labor_
* [House Bill 1131: Licensed estheticians and electrologists](https://click.subscription.in.gov/?%3D "House Bill 1131: Licensed estheticians and electrologists")
* [House Bill 1302: Various labor and safety matters](https://click.subscription.in.gov/?%3D "HB 1302: Various labor and safety matters")

### [Education and Career Development](https://click.subscription.in.gov/?%3D "Education and Career Development")
* [House Bill 1102: Applied behavioral analysis therapy services](https://click.subscription.in.gov/?%3D "House Bill 1102: Applied behavioral analysis therapy services")
* [House Bill 1137: Foods and beverages on school ](https://click.subscription.in.gov/?%3D "House Bill 1137: Foods and beverages on school property") [property ](https://click.subscription.in.gov/?%3D "propertyHouse Bill 1176: Education matters")
* [House Bill 1176: Education matters](https://click.subscription.in.gov/?%3D "propertyHouse Bill 1176: Education matters")
* [House Bill 1266: Department of education and education matters](https://click.subscription.in.gov/?%3D "House Bill 1266: Department of education and education matters")
* [House Bill 1423: Indianapolis public education corporation](https://click.subscription.in.gov/?%3D "House Bill 1423: Indianapolis public education corporation")

### _Utilities_
* [House Bill 1002: Electric utility affordability](https://click.subscription.in.gov/?%3D "House Bill 1002: Electric utility affordability")
* [House Bill 1368: Carbon](https://click.subscription.in.gov/?%3D "House Bill 1368: Carbon")

**Thank you to all the folks who came out and testified in these committees. **

This process only works when the people that legislation will actually impact come out to make their voices heard.

**Bills passed out of these committees next go in front of the entire Senate to be potentially amended on second reading and then voted on for a final time on third reading. **

Stream committees and follow along with legislation at: **[iga.in.gov](https://click.subscription.in.gov/?%3D "iga.in.gov")**
* * *

# **It's Not Too Late to End the Period Tax in Indiana**
---
| [ ](https://click.subscription.in.gov/?%3D)
---
On the Senate floor, I offered an amendment to a piece of legislation with $250 million in tax changes.

**The amendment? To end the period tax in Indiana, a change that would cost Indiana less than $6 million. **

My colleagues on the other side of the aisle said this language was non-germane, or not relevant to the legislation:_not true. _

Did you know one in four teenagers who menstruate cannot afford menstrual products?

Or that 44% of teens report stress and embarrassment due to a lack of access to period products?

It is far past time we address that. **Acknowledging that these are not luxury goods and treating menstrual products accordingly is how we start.

Indiana once again has the chance this legislative session to join the majority of states that treat menstrual products as a necessity. **

### **It is time. **

A single donation can save three lives, and I'm incredibly grateful to everyone who showed up to make a difference.

You can find _[AES's program here](https://click.subscription.in.gov/?%3D "https://urldefense.com/v3/__https://www.aesindiana.com/payment-assistance__;!!FlTQaCg!jwpfitqHKx4bP-5cnhYvoAX1m8Q0kv3P901-pv7dMHXQdpRgas_bRhhF66AOaSuHe8tMuc2p6moGi_XjArAanOEmX3Q$") [.](https://click.subscription.in.gov/?%3D "https://urldefense.com/v3/__https:/www.nipsco.com/bills-and-payments/financial-support__;!!FlTQaCg!i0IlNmwztWy24u3OfjflEyvBopYLxqtX54ZBOGpkRIGHfA-g0F4tvn2RkRjwIClxVywwPaZ8QxM8BqUkhHfV2_ol6Q$")_

As a reminder, the winter moratorium runs from December 1 through March 15 and prevents disconnection of residential energy utility service to any customer who is eligible for and has applied for the Energy Assistance Program. Moratorium protection applies once a household submits an application and allows the Local Service Provider time to determine eligibility.

Utility bills continue to rise, and what should be an essential service has become an overwhelming burden for many families. If you're eligible, please take advantage of the available resources so you don't have to choose between keeping food on the table and keeping the lights on.

Michigan Needs a Prosecutor, Not an Activist
| | |

---
| | Friends,
As Michigan Republicans prepare to select our nominee for Attorney General, it is critical that we look closely at how the current Attorney General is using the power and resources of that office.
[Attorney General Dana Nessel has announced the launch of a so called "Federal Action Tracker,"](https://jrhsf9hbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001Ledhx1yDAaN5X5p_7AZc_Ww_bQzIZ3lRUFoyueFzbxPMrXaAu83DFJ7WYhkrOmHc39J1MC-_3G5bgQMkSjhKSv3zD1wUncVCAXWZCO6FwmpzmYcz9Urgdk5dPQgUzgDWffy9xBWf0ShKfyjLoNRtDFo1GilwDcFsXBQit1VF5jp6pCsa0LV6oMB7ky08X7s5iW5-QsKNGUB_m-DTJfJv5B0ijfCTvWC-dUCFNt7WRxM0dKDmyiBIXAMWGvXofvqHWAhRY754LEFQ6vB0e6BDh4AWYSynh2ZqeZVbF5nbAbnPsAraNSFKlA==&c=OoC5tS21jpbK6ZKPXTYKtHgF_g0rhlM4RrRilNyZjW3-ob5Gk2W4-g==&ch=y8eIXtGi9osja0oTCC_aqGo3zV6gUyuYCQ_Jek86kPZJhzjauEMoHw==) publicly branded as the "Nessel ICE Tracker." This initiative encourages the public to report lawful federal immigration enforcement activity to the Attorney General's office and frames federal law enforcement as a threat to Michigan residents.
As Eaton County Prosecutor and a career prosecutor with decades of experience working alongside local, state, and federal law enforcement, I find this deeply troubling.
Michigan's Attorney General should be defending the rule of law, not politicizing it. The use of state resources to monitor lawful federal enforcement, collect unverified and anonymous submissions, and publicly single out ICE sends a dangerous message. It undermines cooperation between law enforcement agencies and invites interference with officers who are doing their jobs under federal law.
Even more concerning is what this initiative ignores. There is no mechanism to report or deter organized efforts to obstruct federal law enforcement. There is no acknowledgement that today's enforcement actions are the result of failed Biden Harris border policies that left federal agents to clean up the consequences.
Republicans believe in law and order. We believe in accountability. We believe that public safety comes before political theater.
Branding this program as an "ICE Tracker" is not about oversight. It is about activism. Encouraging citizens to monitor and judge federal operations increases the risk of confrontation, endangers officers and the public, and erodes trust between agencies that must work together to keep our communities safe.
Michigan deserves an Attorney General who will restore professionalism, judgment, and respect for the rule of law to the office.
As Republicans, and as delegates entrusted with choosing our nominee, we face a clear choice. We can continue down a path of political stunts and ideological activism, or we can nominate a proven prosecutor who will defend the law without fear or favor.
I am asking for your support as we bring responsible leadership back to the Attorney General's office.
Sincerely,
Doug Lloyd Eaton County Prosecuting Attorney Candidate for Michigan Attorney General

clean_body: Michigan Needs a Prosecutor, Not an Activist | | | | | == | | | == | | Friends, As Michigan Republicans prepare to select our nominee for Attorney General, it is critical that we look closely at how the current Attorney General is using the power and resources of that office. == publicly branded as the "Nessel ICE Tracker." This initiative encourages the public to report lawful federal immigration enforcement activity to the Attorney General's office and frames federal law enforcement as a threat to Michigan residents. As Eaton County Prosecutor and a career prosecutor with decades of experience working alongside local, state, and federal law enforcement, I find this deeply troubling. Michigan's Attorney General should be defending the rule of law, not politicizing it. The use of state resources to monitor lawful federal enforcement, collect unverified and anonymous submissions, and publicly single out ICE sends a dangerous message. It undermines cooperation between law enforcement agencies and invites interference with officers who are doing their jobs under federal law. Even more concerning is what this initiative ignores. There is no mechanism to report or deter organized efforts to obstruct federal law enforcement. There is no acknowledgement that today's enforcement actions are the result of failed Biden Harris border policies that left federal agents to clean up the consequences. Republicans believe in law and order. We believe in accountability. We believe that public safety comes before political theater. Branding this program as an "ICE Tracker" is not about oversight. It is about activism. Encouraging citizens to monitor and judge federal operations increases the risk of confrontation, endangers officers and the public, and erodes trust between agencies that must work together to keep our communities safe. Michigan deserves an Attorney General who will restore professionalism, judgment, and respect for the rule of law to the office. As Republicans, and as delegates entrusted with choosing our nominee, we face a clear choice. We can continue down a path of political stunts and ideological activism, or we can nominate a proven prosecutor who will defend the law without fear or favor. I am asking for your support as we bring responsible leadership back to the Attorney General's office. Sincerely, Doug Lloyd Eaton County Prosecuting Attorney Candidate for Michigan Attorney General 👉 == | | | | | == == == == == == == == == == == == == * | | | | == == == == | | | | | == | | | | Doug Lloyd for MI Attorney General | PO Box, 80536 | Lansing, MI 48906 US | | | | | | | |

Check your ballot at [MyVote.wi.gov](https://republicanpartyofwisconsin.cmail20.com/t/y-l-ayhnkk-didthutlhu-y/), vote early (absentee in-person is underway), or head to the polls on February 17. These elections shape our communities and set the stage for conservative wins statewide. Let's show up strong!-Team WisGOP **The MEGA Act: Restoring Trust in Our Elections** Wisconsin's own Congressman Bryan Steil, as Chairman of the House Administration Committee, recently unveiled the Make Elections Great Again (MEGA) Act. This is a comprehensive, commonsense package of election reforms that sets clear baseline standards for how states run federal elections. The bill aims to boost voter confidence, strengthen election integrity, and ensure our processes remain easy to vote in but hard to cheat. This is a much-needed response to gaps in current federal law, particularly weak enforcement on voter list maintenance, by bringing clarity, accountability, and uniform safeguards nationwide.At its heart, the MEGA Act implements proven, straightforward guidelines: requiring photo ID to vote, verifying citizenship during voter registration, strengthening routine voter roll maintenance to remove ineligible names, mandating that mail-in ballots be received by Election Day, ensuring auditable paper ballots for every vote, and banning risky practices like ballot harvesting, ranked-choice voting, and universal vote-by-mail. These measures build on successful models and align with core GOP priorities to protect the ballot box while keeping participation accessible for lawful American voters.Fair, verifiable elections are the bedrock of our democracy, and clean voter rolls are a legal obligation, not an option. Election security reform is long overdue, and strict rules like those in the MEGA Act are essential to restoring public trust after years of concerns. As Wisconsin conservatives, we applaud Chairman Steil for leading this effort. Let's rally behind the MEGA Act to secure transparent, trustworthy elections for 2026 and beyond! **Take Action!****We need Letter to the Editor Signers!**
Become a Letter to the Editor (LTE) signer and help get the Republican message out to every community across the state. LTE volunteers are critical to continuing to advance our Republican values. Our goal is to have groups in every county who submit LTEs regularly. These groups will have resources provided from our team, including talking points, draft LTEs, and submission instructions. If you have any questions, please reach out to our Communications Director, Anika Rickard, at [arickard@wisgop.org](mailto:arickard@wisgop.org). | | Lifе and death Son of Mykhailo Sulyma, Ivan came from a petty noble (szlachta) family. He was born in Rohoshchi (next to Chernihiv). He served as an estate overseer for Stanisław Żółkiewski and later the family of Daniłowicze who inherited his lands; for that service in 1620 he was awarded three villages: Sulimówka, Kuczakiw and Lebedyn. Аll the villages todаy belong to the Boryspil Raion, Kyiv Oblast. His sons included Stepan (died 1659), a captain of Boryspil company, and Fedir (died 1691), a colonel of Pereiaslav regiment. He became popular among the unregistered Cossacks, leading them on campaigns to plunder Crimea and other Ottoman vassal territories. For organizing a revolt on an Ottoman slave galley and freeing Christian slaves[1] he received a medal from Pope Paul V himself. Eventually, Sulyma reached the rank of the hetman, which he held from 1628 to 1629 and 1630 to 1635. In 1635, after returning from an expedition to Black Sea against the Ottomans, he decided to rebel against the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth, which at that time controlled most of the Cossack territories, and whose nobility was trying to turn militant Cossacks into serfs.[citation needed] Ivan Sulyma took part in numerous campaigns of Sagaidachny against Tatars and Turks. In particular, it was the famous capture of Kafa (modern Theodosia), the main center of the slave trade on the Black Sea, Trapezont, Izmail, and also two attacks on Tsaregrad. On the night of 3 to 4 August 1635 he took the newly constructed Kodak fortress by surprise, burning it and executing its crew of about 200 people under Jean Marion. Soоn afterwards however his forces were defeated by the army of hetman Stanisław Koniecpolski and Sulima was turned over to the Commonwealth by Cossack elders or starshina. Together with several other leaders of his rebellion, Hetman Sulyma was executed in Warsaw on 12 December 1635. At first, the Polish King Władysław IV Waza, known for his friendly attitude towards the Cossacks, was hesitant to execute Sulyma, especially since he was a person upon whom the Pope himself bestowed his medal. However, pressured by the nobility who wanted to show that no rebellions against the 'established оrder' would be tolerated, the оrder for an execution was given; after being tortured, Sulyma was cut to pieces and his body parts were hung on the city walls of Warsaw

Egyptian hieroglyphs were the formal writing system used in Ancient Egypt for writing the Egyptian language. Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. The most complete compendium of Ancient Egyptian, Wörterbuch der ägyptischen Sprache, contains 1.5–1.7 millin words.[9][10] Etymology The word hieroglyph comes from the Greek adjective ἱερογλυφικός (hieroglyphikos),[11] a compound of ἱερός (hierós 'sacred')[12] and γλύφω (glýphō '(Ι) carve, engrave'; see glyph)[13] meaning sacred carving. The glyphs themselves, since the Ptolemaic period, were called τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ [γράμματα] (tà hieroglyphikà [grámmata]) "the sacred engraved letters", the Greek counterpart to the Egyptian expression of mdw.w-nṯr "god's words".[14] Greek ἱερόγλυφος meant "a carver of hieroglyphs".[15] In English, hieroglyph as a noun is recorded from 1590, originally short for nominalized hieroglyphic (1580s, with a plural hieroglyphics), from adjectival use (hieroglyphic character).[16][17] The Nag Hammadi texts written in Sahidic Coptic cal the hieroglyphs "writings of the magicians, soothsayers" (Coptic: ϩⲉⲛⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ ⲡⲣⲁⲛ︦ϣ︦).[18]

Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. The glyphs themselves, since the Ptolemaic period, were called τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ [γράμματα] (tà hieroglyphikà [grámmata]) "the sacred engraved letters", the Greek counterpart to the Egyptian expression of mdw.w-nṯr "god's words".[14] Greek ἱερόγλυφος meant "a carver of hieroglyphs".[15] In English, hieroglyph as a noun is recorded from 1590, originally short for nominalized hieroglyphic (1580s, with a plural hieroglyphics), from adjectival use (hieroglyphic character).[16][17] The Nag Hammadi texts written in Sahidic Coptic cal the hieroglyphs "writings of the magicians, soothsayers" (Coptic: ϩⲉⲛⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ ⲡⲣⲁⲛ︦ϣ︦).[18] | | | | | | “Florida Dad” Gas Station Scene In a viral moment, a Florida dad’s gas station transaction just revealed a secret wealth method—captured on hidden camera for all to see. Kaley Chiles stood alongside her ADF attorneys to challenge a Colorado law that censors her speech in counseling conversations. It forbids licensed counselors like Kaley from having conversations that could help clients regain comfort with their sex--_even if that 's the client's goal._

It's a clear violation of the First Amendment. But this case also points to a much deeper, spiritual battle.

Laws like this one allow lies to spread--lies like one's sex can be changed and God makes mistakes with His creation. These laws suppress truth from going forward by forbidding people like Kaley from speaking it in counseling.

Kaley is stepping up to challenge this law. And a win in her case could help roll back similar laws in 22 other states.

**I want you to think about that for a moment. One young woman 's courageous stand could reach countless lives with the truth.**

I've had the privilege of getting to know Kaley over the last few months, and I have been so encouraged by her unwavering hope in the Lord and commitment to the truth.

It's not been an easy road. The law threatens exorbitant fines and even loss of her license if she follows the truth in the counseling room and helps young clients pursue alignment of their identity with their body. She's also facing tremendous backlash for choosing to push back on this law--and more is sure to come.

Our enemy, the father of lies, will work to oppose the truth and those who speak it at every turn.

But your prayers can make a difference. Will you please pray...
* **For Kaley** --that God would strengthen and encourage her, and that she would sense His peace in the months to come as we await the Court's decision

* **For our culture** --that God would use this case to open more eyes to the harms of gender ideology, and that hearts would turn toward the truth of knowing Him

## School Choice Applications Break Record
More than 42,000 students applied for Texas Education Freedom Accounts (TEFA) the first day enrollments opened, shattering the [national record](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJyk0L2ypSAMwPGnwQ4nRIRrQbGN3d12SwchKjMoDnC-3n7Hc7bY_vZJJv_fn-_p24YYjvW33cnU55Kmgx4lUq2Up-K2lKLbUnBkzzMGZ2tIRykTAioOyEFP3ob4mmTjzQx-EA0ZoTVI1WsQzWa-rCJUEmetejnPIMGSg0GLBaRTPTTBXMcAQQsE0Q2tcLNE8Gixg172PZNAPtSU27pRpactS3ylO-XWpb2JZqv1LKz7xXBkOLq0nzWnGCm37-F2TXeGo53TrTIcd_LBckdHpcxwvGoZjv9e6Pl7hZfNXgCFZ3Ipe76kzEu9eToq_x-Ch4Mf9OAfKP6R4mdOa7Y7vxw6IaTCQX812fjzEWIMRWkmYd1tiO-C-jP3u8G_AQAA___qj5gO) for a new school choice program by surpassing Tennessee’s 33,000 mark from last year. Acting State Comptroller Kelly Hancock said 20,000 families applied for the program within three hours of opening. As application numbers continue to climb, some private schools are [opting out](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkLGOgzAMhp8mbCDHJIQOGW5h6603ojRxS6SUIOKD9u1PtOoT3OjPsvV__895PLuY4nz7dney_Ljmcaa9JGKmdSx-yjn5KUdPbllS9I5jnksZEbCrAWswY3AxPUdVBXuBcJIVWWkMqE4bkNVkDUEfei1BaxlOiL0KSlMwZPrWdZ2uoj2eAYKRCLI9NdJfFEJAhy1opbVQQCFyXhueiOnhyjU980Zr4_O9SnZiXopovwQOAod93xt_KYfFsRc4vE4EDgf6jPVbrX671csaN8f0oVv-9ROtpZ4z1857WjjON4FDtdqw7DGlWDojFNzuLqZXDP5feZvFvwAAAP__xduFGw), saying there are too many unanswered questions about how the program will work. Over 80% of applicants plan to attend private schools through the program, while just under 20% are considering alternatives such as homeschooling. Enrollment in the program runs through March 17, and openings are not filled on a first-come, first-served basis.
## Cowboys to Play in Rio
The Dallas Cowboys will play in the first NFL regular-season game held in [Rio de Janeiro](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkDHPpCAQQH8NdphxQHELimvo9torDcq4zgXFAFnXf3_Z-wtf_ZKXl_fnOT09Rz5ev_1Otn7WNB10lUi1Up7KsqUUly3xQv48Iy--cjpKmRBwkIASzBQ8x3vSTbAzhEfXkO2MAT30BrpmszCS7zulRmMCjL1GPRAOtGplSA0wN2y_MkAwHUKnHm23zBohoEcFve57oYEC15TbulGljy9rvNObcrukvYl2q_UsQv0S6AS667paKufxhQLdsUaBrtSUb4FuEug4CHTajFqZEQS6JV1zuos8o7_lsUa5ci5VvvxOMnOSgeRffxDn1GQbzotj5DIYoeG1e47_I-rP1r0t_gsAAP__2GSBLQ), marking the team's first international game since 2014. Historic Maracana Stadium, the site of the opening ceremony for the 2016 Summer Olympics, will host the game as part of an international slate of NFL games in Paris, Munich, Madrid, London, Mexico City, and Melbourne. It's the third year in a row that an NFL game will be played in Brazil. Sao Paulo hosted games in 2024 and 2025. The Rio matchup will be considered a [home game](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkD1u6zAQhE8jdRSWK0qyCxavUefXphT4s7IYrEWBZEw7pw_sHCHNAAMMBjPfx2W5mMBhv_43N9LlscZlp5qZSqG0ZLfFyG6LwZE5Dg7OlBD3nBcEHAWggGnxJvBzUa3XFvxZtqTlNIEahwlku-lBwiqVH88I9qR6sFb1EvoRxlNPEqc26FcZIEwSQfbnTjqrEDwa7GFQw9AoIB9KTF3ZqNDD5JWf8U6pc_HWst5KOXLT_2twbnCutXbO5nzEVPIr0eC8r_xSqvnXiBSi8CQ-zU4hRWGT-Q4svGE2WbhYbXxm8f6Y3Ub-i6nBuU3aHzUwhzxOjYLrzQR-byh_I3fX-BMAAP__AkiCDQ) for the Cowboys, and their opponent will be announced this spring.

# Saturday, February 7, 2026

**Good morning!** On this day in 1904, a discarded cigarette in Baltimore's business district ignited the Great Baltimore Fire, which burned for 31 hours and destroyed 80 blocks. Officials reported that 1,500 buildings were lost, but fortunately, there were no fatalities. [You can view a collection of photos of the fire here](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLFu8yAURp8Gb7Eu19jEA8O_sOVfO1oUrm3aa4iAJM3bV626dO766dM50nm5LBcXOabtvzvItDUviR6VqTUqSyu341o-2N2S32vL_r3W7IpLCwJOJ8AT6CW4yM9FdcGsREhDR0ZqDWqaEMZuNzSOXkq1kpOSZu29k-ho0DNNZz0q6KL5ogGCligBhv4MYZ2n8zSDUkqrIBRQiC2X_i3H1HZa-ZnvVHqfj47N3tq1iuGfQCvQ-sxMvsWcah_iFpvjw5UnuxT6XDaB9mf99RVoj_C6CrQxCLR61gJtIS_Qyq6YcH1E5lgnLRRsh4v87W5_CnY3-BkAAP__fGd_OQ). Today, as promised, _The Flyover_ introduces its _2026 Winter Olympics_ special section as [Friday's opening ceremony unfolded in Italy](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLHOpCAQgJ9GO8w4sqAFxTV2_7VXGhYG5Q7BALueb39xk3uCv5vkyzeZb359LV_aBx_Xn3onVV1aIp0lUK2Ul5pf-5H_Bv2KZis1mT-lJJ11XBBQMEAGcrHah2vhrVWOCGloSfVSAhcC4dFuyqIEAZOTg32IcTJC0NBrcA65doBT69W9DRBkjz3A0I1g3SRGMQHnXHLbcCDra8rd7-Rj3ciFK70pdybtbVBbrUdphh8Nzg3O53l28Wnuips3OJcj5VoanFO49sObewz-TewZ0nobPlbK7D9ln7Z0UPRxZYYy7SlebPdBR_bxXofVlQrLJmp8yF6ObVb2OH0IvgjZcFh37cPnvPqtn74V_gsAAP__69-MwQ). This is where you can keep up with daily news from the Olympics, including the athletes, events, and even an ongoing medal count for U.S. teams. You'll find it just past the _Sports_ section in today's edition. **Housekeeping note:** _The Flyover_ team finished a productive annual meeting this week, and the team is heading back to their home states to resume regular service. |

## Trump Officially Unveils TrumpRx.gov
President Trump on Feb. 5 launched TrumpRx.gov, a government-backed site [offering 40 discounted prescription drugs](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0LHOnDAQBOCnMZ3RshgDhYtIEd1F6VIig5djE4ORbY7w9tGd8gZ_PdJovvn1GB-WPe_PH3Yjk5cw7nQlTzlTHHM8tyP-9fbc5zXlMP9JKdho9xEBtQSU0I7Osr9HVTizECHVBZmqbUFpjdAUq1Hd0kNVIfSuryerOnAaHBG0sHRqago27zZAaCusAOqyA7f0utM9KKVa5YQCcpxDLH8H3vNKi7_Di2I5h63wZs35SKL-JnAQONhpfgvKZ3jHAoefwXPmOQkcPh557i9iL__j5EVT4kzSbhR5tnuS03lLHy6K8og8kxM4pBziLeqBnai_V9h3faOhKaJxx8Xec9KtUPDcLPvPqvylK18G_wUAAP__4J6I5g) to Americans paying cash, calling it a major step to curb U.S. price disparities nationwide. The administration says “most-favored-nation” deals with 16 major drugmakers will bring U.S. prices down to the lowest paid abroad, cutting Medicaid costs for cash buyers, too. TrumpRx lists about 40 drugs, showing savings and generating pharmacy coupons or directing users to mail-order options. Discounts do not apply to insurance and generally won’t count toward deductibles today. Officials highlighted [lower prices for GLP-1 weight-loss drugs, inhalers, HIV, diabetes,](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkDGy3CAQRE8jZWwhhGA3IHCy2XfqUMXCII2NQMWMVv_f3iXbN3DWQderfv3jY_7wmLEs3_0GjlOdC5yUgRnazO3Y9vaZ_VHCSlzDL6Lqmy-zksoIqYS0c_SYv2bdR5cAFIw9uMFaqY1RcupXl7R6eZPMfZimaRjtffTBQoLHa3xMXuke3UWTStpBDVKOt7uM6WHu5iG11lbHTkuIyLXdflYsvELKX_UN7Rbq1me3Mu_Ujd869ezU8zzPW6qfr4OwANHV6dRzrxkZA12xAWGEwuKvF5D45ymW-hYnvAgZRE0JGpZF-A0aBl9IRKRQj8IQxQUJDXfGWkRsxyL2hgFIrEhcG4a-ubifmDOSsZ2Wy-Yx_xnM__Xy26nfAQAA__-b-peO) and IVF medications. Experts praised the one-stop coupon hub, but noted the list is limited and savings vary overall.
## Three fans, 60 Years of Super Bowls
Three lifelong football fans—the last remaining members of the “never missed a Super Bowl” club [dating back to Super Bowl I in 1967](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLFytCAURp8GO5zrlQUtKP7G6t80KVI6KBclQXGAXePbZzavkPqb-c6c83Ef78YHvy9vZiNdXBx3OnOgUiiNJT22I30H89jnNZc4f-UcTTL7iICSA3JQozU-XKOorHZESG1FulEKhJQIt2rVrpvN7HoBZu6NacCKW99NFltqRTtJqLx-vQGCarABaOsOrOtlJ3sQQihhmQCyvsRUf0a_l5VcuOKTUj3HrQp6LeXIrP3HcGA4mGl-GdRLfM0Mh__eUS5XIIbD6RO9l5guhkPLndkzl8Dz46DEp3iGzIvfiE9-4YvZiDfY902jOlUlbY_Th-CzVEzAshkffvnlT9GeGn8CAAD__1v8gFU)—are returning this Sunday for the 2026 game, and it will probably be the last time as a group. Don Crisman of Maine, nearing 90, and Tom Henschel of Florida, 84 and recovering from a stroke, said this trip will l[ikely end their streaks at 60 straight Super Bowls.](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykUDuO3DAMPY3caUDTWtlTqEijbtOmNGiLHiurkQYSvRPfPnCukIbgAx7e79fn_Ekxxfz4SU92spU587slFuE6Sz2er_on0ZHXvUlZv1orVCnPCGg1oIZxDhTTOZsuuI0ZeejY9eMIxlqEj253C0-TXXtajAVchs3cAywUemS2E3-ELrpLDRDGHnuA4TZB2O52sncwxowmKAMcopR6-11ilp23dJZvrre1PLvkdpFXU8MPhV6hzySxZEpSAp0XQ6E_mkK_kkLfKAvpNVG90FVVob_sFXrA61zfoDfKTZMI56AtyK6bVIqPXXQ7Xlz1Ut5Jp_jF6dSyc6w6UROFvqsuvN4xpdjsqAw8nhTTv6DyX-t-O_wbAAD__1cDjf4) Gregory Eaton of Michigan, 86, says he plans to keep attending as long as he’s physically able, still hoping to one day see the Detroit Lions reach the game. He remains the only one still working. _“I think all of them are big, they're all fun. It's just gotten so commercial. It's a $10,000 trip now,”_ Eaton said.
| _Flying together with our sponsor_ [](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkTGP3CAQhX8N7ryCgcV24SLSyd2lTYnmYFiTw2DB3F3u30e7SlKmuXY033uf9H48u2dMOZXbdzxo5VhdoY-eiZma4_Z2nO1Xxrfi987Vv_ZesWFxIMGOEkY5uYApfzozhDUSAemBVjVN0lgL8jrsK80Kl1kZH6yMpBQiGQXK-hCtUi_TkNZ7mgQ5KVBS6sssQ1zsbBdpjJlMEEZSSFzb5WdNhXeK-bO-U7v4egx53ZnPLvQ3AZuAjRv617-PmHn3tcQUqHDCfCcEbFKpyVqjx0V7GI0K13HxBCPOFOOi5ayuKPR2ZvR0UGGhn_5Uun7W0mtzB6bi7s5gBVgMKQj95HdMLddyE2D5cQmpkecX9x_c_aOGtobzI-Wcup2EkbcD00N54C8t877C7wAAAP__g_OjDw) **Why Getting Up From A Chair Gets Harder Each Year (It's Not Age)** How do some folks stay active well into their 70s, 80s, and even 90s... while others find themselves hobbling down stairs or needing to rock back and forth just to get out of a chair? According to a breakthrough discovery by Harvard University scientists, it comes down to a hidden culprit that dries out your joints from the inside: "joint drought." When this "drought" is addressed, it not only soothes joint discomfort but makes joints feel younger and more mobile than they have in years. name: Douglas Carswell
subject: Did the Senate kill School Choice in Mississippi?
body:
| | | [View this email in your browser](https://mailchi.mp/mspolicy/hb2parentpower-12851866?e=5703353baa)
---
| |
---
| _**If you're not in front of our Saturday email, you're behind.**_
---
| Dear Friend,
**Lt Gov Delbert Hosemann and Senator Dennis DeBar manoeuvred to kill the school choice bill, HB2, this week.** They moved against parent power using a Senate education committee procedure, taking less than 90 seconds and not allowing any debate.

**Governor Tate Reeves spoke for many in our state when he said he has “never been more disappointed in elected officials than I am this morning in LG Hosemann and Senator Dennis Debar.”**
---
|
---
_Hosemann & DeBar kill core conservative policy_
| Hosemann and Debar “killed a Republican legislative priority shared by conservatives all across this country and they worked closely with the Democrats to do it. Even worse - they tried to do it in the dark and hide it from MS conservatives on a deadline day.”

The following day, Senator Nicole Boyd was on Supertalk suggesting school choice is ‘not conservative’. Do her primary voters know?

So, what now?

1. **Don’t be distracted by chaff**

**Anxious not to be exposed as un-conservative, the Senate leadership has passed a range of education bills that are the legislative equivalent of chaff** – those clouds of particles fired from military aircraft to distract the enemy radar.

There are Senate bills in favor of math and civics. (Great). There’s a bill to allow students to switch schools, but only if they come from an F rated district, two years in a row. (Ok. Sort of). There are even bills in favor of motherhood and apple pie. (Just kidding.)

None of the chaff bills are disagreeable (in fact most should be supported). But they do nothing to actually empower parents. Mississippi parents – unlike families in each of our surrounding states – would not be able to control their child’s share of the state funds.

**Do not accept the claim that the Senate is somehow advancing school choice with education bills that do not give parents power.**

1. **Resurrect school choice – and send it back to the Senate.**

Over the past two years the House passed a flagship conservative policy – income tax elimination and before that school funding reform. Each time the Senate moved to kill the policy, and each time the House came back. There then followed a battle of wills, which the House won.

**Speaker Jason White, who has invested political capital in school choice, could do something similar this time. Amending one of the Senate chaff bills to include the key parts of HB2 – and sending it back - would be one way to do it.**

The danger is that some might try to only include some of the less important parts of HB2. An education freedom bill that does not allow families to control their share of the budget is not an education freedom bill.

What if that fails?

1. **A Special Session**

**Governor Tate Reeves has been so robust in his condemnation of Delbert Hosemann, I wonder if he might be willing to call a Special Session** \- unless Hosemann starts to support mainstream Republican party education policy.

Calling a Special Session unless a law allowing education freedom is passed would be a powerful tool. The Governor could set the agenda. The spotlight would be on Mr. Hosemann, and if he and his sidekicks really were willing to block parent power, the entire state would be able to see. A bold move for someone said to still harbor gubernatorial ambition, perhaps.

**This week was a step back for school choice, but we had similar reversals when the Senate leadership tried to stop previous reforms.**

We lost a battle for parent power this week. We can win the fight. But perhaps the key lesson is that those wanting school choice need to understand that we do actually need to fight.

**Nicey nicey only encouraged them to kill the bill without debate. **
---

Douglas Carswell

Speaker Jason White, who has invested political capital in school choice, could do something similar this time. Amending one of the Senate chaff bills to include the key parts of HB2 – and sending it back - would be one way to do it. The danger is that some might try to only include some of the less important parts of HB2. An education freedom bill that does not allow families to control their share of the budget is not an education freedom bill. What if that fails? 1. A Special Session Governor Tate Reeves has been so robust in his condemnation of Delbert Hosemann, I wonder if he might be willing to call a Special Session \- unless Hosemann starts to support mainstream Republican party education policy. Calling a Special Session unless a law allowing education freedom is passed would be a powerful tool. The Governor could set the agenda. The spotlight would be on Mr. Hosemann, and if he and his sidekicks really were willing to block parent power, the entire state would be able to see. A bold move for someone said to still harbor gubernatorial ambition, perhaps. This week was a step back for school choice, but we had similar reversals when the Senate leadership tried to stop previous reforms. We lost a battle for parent power this week. We can win the fight. But perhaps the key lesson is that those wanting school choice need to understand that we do actually need to fight. Nicey nicey only encouraged them to kill the bill without debate. | "Forward this email to a friend!" | | Warm regards, Douglas Carswell President & CEO | | |

body:
[ stdin# ][IMG]

NEWS FROM THE POLITICAL REVOLUTION

HEADLINES: Defund Oligarchs, Fund the People | ICE Out Now! |
Frontline Report from MN | Rashida Joins Our Fight | Must-Win
Midterms | Exciting New Endorsements | & MORE!

★ ★ ★

OUR MISSION

ICE is terrorizing our communities, Trump and his oligarchs are
pillaging our democracy, and WE ARE NOT BACKING DOWN.

Our movement is stronger than ever, and fighting on every front:
legislatively, electorally, and in the streets. This is a moment for
strength and strategy — and we’re grateful to have you in this fight.

Our Revolution is focused on building grassroots power to Fight Trump
& the Oligarchs with our 3 Point Strategy:

1.
1. Fight Trump’s Oligarch Agenda - from Capitol Hill to City
Halls
2. Elect Anti-Oligarch Champions up and down the ballot
3. Get Oligarch Money out of Politics and uplift the
grassroots

Read below to learn how we’re carrying out our mission - and [ https://act.ourrevolution.com/go/35232?t=1011&akid=10187%2E5885482%2E0Wilcj ]chip
in a donation to fuel this people-powered resistance.

★ ★ ★

[2]Fight Trump & The Oligarchs

★ ★ ★

Our Revolution is teaming-up with US Reps. Rashida Tlaib, Pramila
Jayapal and others on a new Congressional resolution to Defund the
Oligarchs and Fund the People.

Trump returned to power promising to “drain the swamp” and fight for
working people — instead he’s turning our government into a personal
ATM to enrich his oligarch donors and his own family.

New research from Our Revolution, first reported by [ https://act.ourrevolution.com/go/35233?t=1012&akid=10187%2E5885482%2E0Wilcj ]The Guardian,
shows that Trump’s mega-donors from the crypto, oil and gas, and
private detention industries poured nearly $700 million into electing
him and MAGA.

Since then, they’ve raked in more than $170 billion in tax breaks,
government contracts, and policy favors. That’s an 18,000% return on
investment — or $18 billion back for every $1 million spent in the
2024 election.

[ https://act.ourrevolution.com/go/35234?t=1013&akid=10187%2E5885482%2E0Wilcj ]WATCH THE DEFUND OLIGARCHY VIDEO!

Our campaign isn’t just about exposing corruption — it’s about ending
corporate control of our government and cutting off the pipelines
that turn political power into private profit.

This is a massive effort to fundamentally restructure our political
economy. With our allies in Congress and our grassroots movement
working together, we can make real change. [ https://act.ourrevolution.com/go/35232?t=1014&akid=10187%2E5885482%2E0Wilcj ]Chip in any amount to
help fund the activists and organizers doing this essential work.

“This resolution is an organizing and education tool to expose the
truth: our democracy is being sold to the highest bidder,” Rep.
Rashida Tlaib told over 100,000 people joining our [ https://act.ourrevolution.com/go/35235?t=1015&akid=10187%2E5885482%2E0Wilcj ]Live Organize
to Win Town Hall. “Ending the oligarchy’s power is crucial — it’s
how we fight for working people.”

[ https://act.ourrevolution.com/go/35236?t=1016&akid=10187%2E5885482%2E0Wilcj ]Read The Guardian op-ed with Rep. Rashida Tlaib and Our
Revolution's Joseph Geevarghese here.

“Look at the for-profit scheme behind ICE and Border Patrol —
corporations are making billions detaining our children and tearing
families apart,” [ https://act.ourrevolution.com/go/35237?t=1017&akid=10187%2E5885482%2E0Wilcj ]she said.

Take GEO Group and CoreCivic, the two largest private prison
contractors. Our research shows they poured nearly $5 million into
Trump and GOP campaigns — and have since seen an obscene 11,050%
return as detention and deportation expand. [ https://act.ourrevolution.com/go/35238?t=1018&akid=10187%2E5885482%2E0Wilcj ]Read more in Jacobin.

Our Revolution organizer Dieu Do also joined our live call to give a
report from the frontlines in Minneapolis, where she has been helping
lead the grassroots resistance to ICE.

“I’ve watched protesters be brutalized with tear gas, pepper spray,
and flashbangs simply for exercising their constitutional rights,”
[ https://act.ourrevolution.com/go/35239?t=1019&akid=10187%2E5885482%2E0Wilcj ]she said. “We’ve seen children detained and used as bait to lure
family members out of their homes.”

“What stands out just as much as the cruelty is the solidarity —
communities organizing patrols, mutual aid, and legal observers to
keep neighbors safe,” Dieu continued. “This is a watershed moment —
more people than ever are asking why their tax dollars are funding
terror instead of healthcare, housing, and education.”

[ https://act.ourrevolution.com/go/35240?t=1020&akid=10187%2E5885482%2E0Wilcj ]Add your name to pressure Congress to Defund ICE.

And pick up one of our new Break ICE stickers to help us fund our
frontline work on the ground in Minneapolis and across the country.
It’s up to us to stand up for our communities and our neighbors.

[ https://act.ourrevolution.com/go/35241?t=1021&akid=10187%2E5885482%2E0Wilcj ]GET YOUR STICKER

★ ★ ★

Learn more about our research and the campaign at our new [ http://act.ourrevolution.com/go/35242?t=1022&akid=10187%2E5885482%2E0Wilcj ]Defund
Oligarchy website and sign on to be a [ https://act.ourrevolution.com/go/35243?t=1023&akid=10187%2E5885482%2E0Wilcj ]Citizen Cosponsor of the
resolution to push more members of Congress to publicly support it.

★ ★ ★

TAKING ON CORPORATIONS COMPLICIT WITH ICE

Across the nation, Our Revolution activists and our allies are
ramping up grassroots pressure to stop corporations from
collaborating with the Trump regime to terrorize our communities and
target our neighbors.

In St. Louis, we protested outside the headquarters of Entreprise
Rent-a-Car, a privately held company that does over $80 million a
year in business with federal agencies, including Homeland Security.

No corporation should be helping masked ICE agents hunt down our
neighbors and brutalize our people. We will keep up the backlash and
public pressure for Enterprise and other complicit companies to do
the right thing.

This work takes resources, but we’re not backing down. Our
communities are relying on us, and we’re relying on grassroots
donations to make it happen. [ https://act.ourrevolution.com/go/35232?t=1024&akid=10187%2E5885482%2E0Wilcj ]Donate $10 or any amount to make a
difference!

In the Bay Area, Our Revolution protested outside Palantir’s Palo
Alto office Thursday to expose how the company is cashing in on ICE
surveillance and repression.

As Palantir’s stock soars on lucrative government contracts, our
activists are calling out a system that uses public dollars to fund
mass surveillance, target immigrants, and endanger communities.

“The Defund the Oligarchs, Fund the People resolution is about taking
our tax dollars back from billionaires like Peter Thiel and
corporations like Palantir — and stopping companies that are
profiting off harm to our communities,” Our Revolution East Bay
co-chair Susana Williams told [ https://act.ourrevolution.com/go/35244?t=1025&akid=10187%2E5885482%2E0Wilcj ]American Community Media.

VICTORY! Avelo Airlines cuts ties with ICE. Our movement showed up at
airports from California to Maryland, and as a result Avelo Airlines
is grounding ALL of

its deportation flights.

Our activists also joined allies to protest outside AT&T stores in
Chicago — demanding they drop their multimillion-dollar ICE
contracts, profiting from using its tech to help terrorize our
communities.

When corporations align with authoritarian policies, people suffer.
But when we unite as neighbors and movement builders, we make clear
that our collective power is stronger than corporate greed.

[ https://act.ourrevolution.com/go/35232?t=1026&akid=10187%2E5885482%2E0Wilcj ]We take ZERO money from billionaires and big donors. We rely on
the grassroots to keep up this great work. Chip in a donation today!

★ ★ ★

[18]Take Back The Party

★ ★ ★

The 2026 midterms are pivotal to take power back from Trump and the
oligarchs who have rigged our economy and captured our democracy.

We need more fighters in office - each of our candidates have taken
the pledge to Fight Oligarchy in office - and we’re excited to roll
out these new people-powered endorsements for 2026.

Check out our [ https://act.ourrevolution.com/go/35245?t=1027&akid=10187%2E5885482%2E0Wilcj ]Endorsements Page for more!

★ ★ ★

This race is a nail-biter! Analilia Mejia - former political
director for Bernie 2020 - is leading by a few hundred votes with 90%
counted in Thursday’s primary election for the Congress seat in New
Jersey’s 11th District.

A win in this race will send shockwaves through the establishment as
she ran a people-powered campaign against big-money funded opponents.

★ ★ ★

Congrats to Christian Menefee on his victory in the special election
for a Congressional seat representing Texas’ 18th District!

Christian has been a fearless advocate for voting rights,
environmental justice, and holding powerful interests accountable —
now he’s bringing that energy to Capitol Hill!

★ ★ ★

Our Revolution is proud to endorse Nida Allam for Congress in North
Carolina’s 4th District. A longtime movement leader and former
political director for Bernie Sanders’ 2016 campaign, Nida also has
Bernie’s backing in this key 2026 race.

Nida also had our support in her successful run for Durham County
Commission, where she helped raise the minimum wage and expand
funding for immigrant services. As she said on our live organizing
call Monday: “Ending the oligarchy’s power over our country is not a
partisan issue — it’s about how we fight for working people.”

★ ★ ★

Our Revolution proudly endorses Rep. Delia Ramirez for reelection to
Congress. Since taking office, Delia has been a bold leader for
Medicare for All, environmental justice, workers’ rights, and
immigrant dignity.

Delia is also a key partner in our fight to Defund the Oligarchs and
Fund the People, signing on to the resolution and working with us to
confront corporate power.

| Letter from the Chair
---
Why Bother Voting? Addressing the Common Excuses
If you're reading this newsletter, you're likely more engaged in politics than most. You're also probably more inclined to vote when election time rolls around.
Lately, I've been reflecting on the reasons people give for sitting out elections--and how we might thoughtfully respond when friends, family, or neighbors share them. These excuses come up often, especially among people of faith. Here's a closer look at a few, along with some perspective to consider.
"I'm Tired of Voting for the Lesser of Two Evils"
This is one of the most common frustrations: neither candidate feels inspiring, so why choose the "lesser evil"?
Father Chad Ripperger, a respected Catholic priest and theologian, offers a compelling moral framework here. He explains that when you vote in such a scenario, you're not endorsing evil--you're actively working to preserve the good that would be lost if the greater evil prevailed. Failing to act in that situation, allowing the worse outcome by default, can amount to negligence--a sin of omission.
This shifts the focus from "approving" a flawed choice to protecting what's valuable. It's a practical way to navigate imperfect options while staying true to conscience.
"It's in God's Hands--Why Vote at All?"
Some believers see voting as unnecessary because ultimate outcomes rest with God. And it's true: Scripture doesn't command voting, and in the U.S., it's a right, not a legal obligation. No one sins by abstaining purely on those grounds.
Yet faith traditions often highlight positive reasons to participate:
Voting can be an act of charity toward our neighbors--seeking policies that promote human dignity and the common good. It's an exercise in stewardship--using the civic gifts we've been given to help preserve them for future generations.
Of course, some faiths prohibit voting as a matter of conscience, and no one should pressure anyone to go against their deeply held beliefs. But for most people of faith, voting aligns with loving our neighbor and being responsible caretakers.
Imagine if all people of faith in Nebraska stayed home on Election Day. Our small towns, communities, and state policies would look very different--likely shifting in ways that could undermine the values that we hold dear.
"My Vote Doesn't Count Anyway"
With headlines about election irregularities, ballot issues, fraud claims, and more, it's easy to feel disillusioned. Skepticism is understandable.
But look at 2024: President Trump's "too big to rig" strategy--mobilizing massive turnout--demonstrated that winning big is still possible despite challenges. Nebraska and many other places lean strongly one way, yet turnout makes the difference.
Here's the hard truth: Your vote definitely won't count if you don't cast it. If every potential Republican voter showed up consistently, outcomes in Nebraska (and beyond) would be decisive victories.
The Reality of Commitment
Voting is a commitment, and like any commitment, it faces obstacles--bad weather, busy schedules, frustration, or apathy. Some voters are "fair-weather patriots," showing up only when it's convenient. Others vote faithfully every cycle. Most of us fall somewhere in between.
The key is recognizing that consistent participation matters more than perfection. Showing up, even when it's not ideal, is how we influence the direction of our communities and country.
Closing Summary
At its core, voting isn't about finding a flawless hero--it's about protecting the good, stewarding our rights, and loving our neighbors through the choices available to us.
In Nebraska and across the country, high turnout among engaged citizens--including people of faith--would shape outcomes that affect families, communities, and future generations. Your vote is one piece of that puzzle, but when combined with others, it's a catalyst for positive change.

clean_body: News, events, and action items to keep Nebraska red and growing strong. | | | | | | Letter from the Chair Why Bother Voting? Addressing the Common Excuses If you're reading this newsletter, you're likely more engaged in politics than most. You're also probably more inclined to vote when election time rolls around. Lately, I've been reflecting on the reasons people give for sitting out elections--and how we might thoughtfully respond when friends, family, or neighbors share them. These excuses come up often, especially among people of faith. Here's a closer look at a few, along with some perspective to consider. "I'm Tired of Voting for the Lesser of Two Evils" This is one of the most common frustrations: neither candidate feels inspiring, so why choose the "lesser evil"? Father Chad Ripperger, a respected Catholic priest and theologian, offers a compelling moral framework here. He explains that when you vote in such a scenario, you're not endorsing evil--you're actively working to preserve the good that would be lost if the greater evil prevailed. Failing to act in that situation, allowing the worse outcome by default, can amount to negligence--a sin of omission. This shifts the focus from "approving" a flawed choice to protecting what's valuable. It's a practical way to navigate imperfect options while staying true to conscience. "It's in God's Hands--Why Vote at All?" Some believers see voting as unnecessary because ultimate outcomes rest with God. And it's true: Scripture doesn't command voting, and in the U.S., it's a right, not a legal obligation. No one sins by abstaining purely on those grounds. Yet faith traditions often highlight positive reasons to participate: Voting can be an act of charity toward our neighbors--seeking policies that promote human dignity and the common good. It's an exercise in stewardship--using the civic gifts we've been given to help preserve them for future generations. Of course, some faiths prohibit voting as a matter of conscience, and no one should pressure anyone to go against their deeply held beliefs. But for most people of faith, voting aligns with loving our neighbor and being responsible caretakers. Imagine if all people of faith in Nebraska stayed home on Election Day. Our small towns, communities, and state policies would look very different--likely shifting in ways that could undermine the values that we hold dear. "My Vote Doesn't Count Anyway" With headlines about election irregularities, ballot issues, fraud claims, and more, it's easy to feel disillusioned. Skepticism is understandable. But look at 2024: President Trump's "too big to rig" strategy--mobilizing massive turnout--demonstrated that winning big is still possible despite challenges. Nebraska and many other places lean strongly one way, yet turnout makes the difference. Here's the hard truth: Your vote definitely won't count if you don't cast it. If every potential Republican voter showed up consistently, outcomes in Nebraska (and beyond) would be decisive victories. The Reality of Commitment Voting is a commitment, and like any commitment, it faces obstacles--bad weather, busy schedules, frustration, or apathy. Some voters are "fair-weather patriots," showing up only when it's convenient. Others vote faithfully every cycle. Most of us fall somewhere in between. The key is recognizing that consistent participation matters more than perfection. Showing up, even when it's not ideal, is how we influence the direction of our communities and country. Closing Summary At its core, voting isn't about finding a flawless hero--it's about protecting the good, stewarding our rights, and loving our neighbors through the choices available to us. In Nebraska and across the country, high turnout among engaged citizens--including people of faith--would shape outcomes that affect families, communities, and future generations. Your vote is one piece of that puzzle, but when combined with others, it's a catalyst for positive change.
