Peter, As the Winter Olympics get underway, it’s a reminder of the rare moments when sports don’t just entertain us - they bring our country together.

I was honored to have the opportunity to sit down with Mike Eruzione, captain of the 1980 U.S. Olympic hockey team and a central figure in the “Miracle on Ice,” one of the greatest moments in American sports history. In our conversation, we talk about leadership, teamwork, and what it meant to be part of a moment that united Americans and still resonates decades later. I hope you enjoy it!

Hey friend,
Politics can chew you up and spit you out. That’s why the people you meet on the trail matter.
I recently sat down with my friend Josh Cowen, who is a professor of education policy at Michigan State University and an amazing advocate for his community.
He asked me some tough, thoughtful questions on his Substack. I wanted to share the big takeaways here. [https://joshcowen.substack.com/p/we-are-going-to-be-the-party-that]
* People in MI-10 are struggling, and I’m done watching Congress do the same old things while working families fall farther behind. I have enormous respect for what earlier generations built, but systems designed decades ago aren’t working for families today. If Congress keeps telling younger members to “wait their turn,” we’re going to keep failing people who can’t afford to wait.
* I outperformed Kamala Harris and our congressional nominee in this district in 2024 by staying focused on what voters here actually care about—not Washington talking points.
* I’m a mom and a former prosecutor. I know the law, I know how to fight against powerful interests, and I know what families in our community are up against every day. I’ll use my experience to hold corporations accountable, protect working people, and deliver real results instead of excuses.
* I’m a mom on a mission fighting to lower costs, protect our families, and defend our democracy.

body:
The Trump regime has dedicated itself to chipping away at our legacy, rights, and opportunities.

[](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/124918576/600113469/-153530995?refcode=EM_F_260207BHM_N_SB_90DO_5_NG_N_LOGO&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMjEvMS84Nzg0NCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJkYjAwMjJiYS0zNTA0LWYxMTEtODMyZi0wMDBkM2ExZjBlNGMiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=fTqybmv60jwILsvA0-mmhR5zZjcHAPhkfMXY7gtfX7I=) Peter,

Happy Black History Month! This is the time to educate ourselves about how Black Americans played a critical role in the development of our great nation and to speak up about our history and the current fight we’re facing.

**The Trump regime has dedicated itself to chipping away at our legacy, rights, and opportunities.** In fact, one of Donald Trump’s first actions was terminating federal government diversity, equity, and inclusion programs. And then just last month, they moved to erase our history with an executive order to whitewash museums, parks, and landmarks, which resulted in the removal of an exhibit on slavery at Philadelphia’s Independence National Historical Park.

**As a proud member of the Congressional Black Caucus, I am extremely disappointed by the blatant and ongoing attacks on Black Americans and Black communities. Trump will do anything to make America less fair, less just, and less inclusive.**

subject: What They Said Wasn't True — Setting the Record Straight
body:
Pray. Serve. Vote.
| | | February 07, 2026 | [**Read Online**](https://de717de0.click.convertkit-mail2.com/qdunm92pw8f7h4z07odslh8ddxdkkc4hkovx9/58hvh7hg3wp9z2a6/aHR0cHM6Ly9ja2FyY2hpdmUuY29tL2IvNXF1dmg3aG5xenZrZ3NwNXh4ZDUyYTlsbGdsNDRibmhnMG1wbw==) |
---
| Hi Friend — I want to begin by acknowledging something we’re all feeling. We are living through a season of constant disclosure — headline after headline, revelation after revelation. It can be hard to know what’s true, who to trust, and where to place your footing when the ground feels like it’s shifting beneath us. The uncertainty is exhausting. I feel it too. But here is what I’ve learned, time and again, when the chips are down: everyday Americans don’t retreat — we come together. Quietly. Resolutely. Without permission. And when we do, there is very little we cannot accomplish. That truth has carried me through the hardest moments of this work, and it is as reliable as the sun's rising. Goodness will turn up when you least expect it. Stay focused. Lamps full. It will not be easy. But, we are in a season of truth. And with that ... here's the latest:
* * *
**What They Said Wasn't True** Earlier this week, we sent a slew of cease-and-desist letters out. [Here's the one sent to Democracy Docket and its founder, Marc Elias](https://de717de0.click.convertkit-mail2.com/qdunm92pw8f7h4z07odslh8ddxdkkc4hkovx9/48hvhehmw3z2noax/aHR0cHM6Ly90dHYtc2l0ZS5maWxlcy5zdmRjZG4uY29tL3Byb2R1Y3Rpb24vRGVtb2NyYWN5LURvY2tldC1SZXRyYWN0aW9uLUxldHRlci1yZWRhY3RlZC5wZGYucGRmP2RtPTE3NzAzMTkxNTE=). Democracy Docket — along with the Washington Post, NPR, The Independent, and many others — published coordinated stories filled with false claims about True the Vote. They ran simultaneously, all suggesting that because I published a letter calling for DOGE to audit voter rolls, that somehow we were the "unnamed right wing" group referenced in court filings that had been involved in allegedly improper data sharing. Well, we weren't, but that didn't stop the stories from being written. The stories all echoed one another. And every single one of them got the story wrong. That is not journalism. That is narrative enforcement. [Background: Marc Elias is the founder of Democracy Docket. His law firm, Elias Law, represents Stacey Abrams' organization, Fair Fight, in an ongoing lawsuit against us — a case we won in federal court. They appealed to the 11th Circuit, now we are awaiting that court’s decision. Against that backdrop, Democracy Docket launched this attack that blurred facts and relied on insinuation instead of evidence.] So why are they doing this? I believe the broader objective is to condition the public to accept that voter rolls should never be reviewed by anyone except the state itself and the swamp's partisan NGO of choice, ERIC. Lots of datapoints to back up my theory, from lawsuits, to legislation, to legacy media messaging, all promoting the same basic idea that voter rolls shouldn’t be audited because databases aren't perfect and mistakes might be made. That is like saying we should fear the mirror because it might show a flaw. Imperfection is not a reason to avoid oversight — it is the reason oversight exists. We will not accept this false premise. And we will not let lies about our work go unanswered. We'll keep you posted.
* * *
**Kudos to Kevin: Persistence Matters** Kevin Moncla is an independent researcher who became aware of election malfeasance during 2020 and refused to look away. When others moved on, Kevin stayed. When pressure mounted, he persisted. When doors closed, he kept working. [The 263-page report,](https://de717de0.click.convertkit-mail2.com/qdunm92pw8f7h4z07odslh8ddxdkkc4hkovx9/wnh2hghqmd9oo9a7/aHR0cHM6Ly90dHYtc2l0ZS5maWxlcy5zdmRjZG4uY29tL3Byb2R1Y3Rpb24vUmVwb3J0LW9mLUludmVzdGlnYXRpb24tRnVsdG9uLTIwMjAucGRmP2RtPTE3NzAzMTY2NTQ=) principally authored by Kevin, was the result of relentless, disciplined pursuit of truth — supported over years of hard work by outstanding researchers and activists including Joe Rossi, Paul (@ericciaramella), Holly Kessler, Mark Davis, Jason Frazier, VoterGA, Julie Adams, Rochelle Moncla, Garland Favorito, and David Cross; written about by rock-solid citizen journalists like Wendi Mahoney; and championed by Georgia State Election Board beacons Jan Johnson and Salleigh Grubbs. That work formed the probable cause foundation for the FBI’s Fulton County, Georgia raid. What happens next is up to the Bureau. But the truth is no longer hidden. It is emerging — slowly, perhaps — but unmistakably. It is unfortunate to see others now taking credit for the work, even going so far as to reformat the report under different letterhead. The report linked above is the original. A magnum opus. Kudos to them all! Excited to see what's coming next. Truth be told ... I know some of what's coming next and it's going to be a lot of fun. Buckle up.
* * *
**LegiTrack Is Live!** I’m so excited to share this: [**LegiTrack is officially live**](https://de717de0.click.convertkit-mail2.com/qdunm92pw8f7h4z07odslh8ddxdkkc4hkovx9/08hwh9h2n40779hl/bGVnaXRyYWNrLm9yZw==). LegiTrack is a tool for citizens. It’s designed to help everyday Americans track election integrity-related legislation clearly and confidently — without spin, without gatekeepers, and without requiring a law degree to understand what’s happening. This is about more than information. It’s about agency. FUN FACT: Right now, LegiTrack is being tested by a really fun bunch of folks that signed up to help kick tires on the app. If you want early access, deeper involvement, and first looks at the tools we’re building, you can sign up to volunteer here 👉 [**Sign Up!**](https://de717de0.click.convertkit-mail2.com/qdunm92pw8f7h4z07odslh8ddxdkkc4hkovx9/m2h7h5h32xknnnsm/aHR0cHM6Ly90cnVldGhldm90ZS5vcmcvc2lnbi11cA==) | [](https://de717de0.click.convertkit-mail2.com/qdunm92pw8f7h4z07odslh8ddxdkkc4hkovx9/08hwh9h2n40779hl/bGVnaXRyYWNrLm9yZw==)**You can learn more at**[**legitrack.org**](https://de717de0.click.convertkit-mail2.com/qdunm92pw8f7h4z07odslh8ddxdkkc4hkovx9/08hwh9h2n40779hl/bGVnaXRyYWNrLm9yZw==)
---
* * *
**Setting the Record Straight**
You may have seen [**the recent Gateway Pundit article**](https://de717de0.click.convertkit-mail2.com/qdunm92pw8f7h4z07odslh8ddxdkkc4hkovx9/7qh7h8h9dev449fz/aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cudGhlZ2F0ZXdheXB1bmRpdC5jb20vMjAyNi8wMi9pbS10ZWFtLXBsYXllci1zZW5hdG9yLWRhdmlkLXBlcmR1ZS1ncmFuZC1qdXJ5Lw==) detailing events we experienced firsthand in 2020 and 2021, now finally coming to light through Grand Jury testimony.
| | | True the Vote @TrueTheVote
---|---
[Thank you helping get the truth out @canncon The public was told there was no probable cause to investigate our findings. We’d been cancelled across all social media and had almost no voice to fight back. Now, 5 years later, Grand jury testimony exposes what was really going](https://de717de0.click.convertkit-mail2.com/qdunm92pw8f7h4z07odslh8ddxdkkc4hkovx9/z2hghnhe5z9ddwtp/aHR0cHM6Ly94LmNvbS9UcnVlVGhlVm90ZS9zdGF0dXMvMjAxOTQ0Njg0MTY4MzkyNzQ3OD9zPTIw)
4:23 PM • Feb 5, 2026
1918 | Retweets | 4202 | Likes
---|---|---|---
[Read 113 replies](https://de717de0.click.convertkit-mail2.com/qdunm92pw8f7h4z07odslh8ddxdkkc4hkovx9/z2hghnhe5z9ddwtp/aHR0cHM6Ly94LmNvbS9UcnVlVGhlVm90ZS9zdGF0dXMvMjAxOTQ0Njg0MTY4MzkyNzQ3OD9zPTIw)

Basically, it's the story of how politicos and power brokers worked together to ensure our work would not be investigated in Georgia. As public pressure mounted, their focus shifted to blaming us rather than examining our evidence. We knew it was happening, we wrote about it here, but there were very few other outlets available. We were, like many, being sued, deplatformed, and terrorized into silence.
Today's landscape isn't altogether different, but it is so much better now than it was then because now millions more Americans are awake. In fact, [**a recent Rasmussen poll**](https://de717de0.click.convertkit-mail2.com/qdunm92pw8f7h4z07odslh8ddxdkkc4hkovx9/6qheh8hlx4v22zio/aHR0cHM6Ly94LmNvbS93bWFob25leTUvc3RhdHVzLzIwMTk4MDE5NjEyMDY1MjY0MTY_cz00Mg==) shows that the majority of Americans, regardless of political party affiliation, want to the public to be able to inspect election records, and by extension hear the full stories, see the documents, have the facts. This is a great sign! The poll might just as easily have shown that Americans don't really care — turns out, they do!
Keep pressing for truth, wherever it leads. Together, we can handle it.
* * *
**Looking Ahead—and Asking for Your Help**
We are growing our team. We are launching new apps. We are fighting in court. And we are scaling quickly for what lies ahead this election season.
I know resources are tight for many families right now. I don’t ask lightly. [**But if you’re able to donate to True the Vote it would be an enormous help to us.**](https://de717de0.click.convertkit-mail2.com/qdunm92pw8f7h4z07odslh8ddxdkkc4hkovx9/kkhmh6hnzpg99wul/aHR0cHM6Ly90cnVldGhldm90ZS5vcmcvZG9uYXRl)
This work exists because people like you refuse to disengage, even when the noise is loud and the pressure is real.

[Please Help Us Keep Going](https://de717de0.click.convertkit-mail2.com/qdunm92pw8f7h4z07odslh8ddxdkkc4hkovx9/kkhmh6hnzpg99wul/aHR0cHM6Ly90cnVldGhldm90ZS5vcmcvZG9uYXRl)
---
[https://truethevote.org/donate](https://de717de0.click.convertkit-mail2.com/qdunm92pw8f7h4z07odslh8ddxdkkc4hkovx9/kkhmh6hnzpg99wul/aHR0cHM6Ly90cnVldGhldm90ZS5vcmcvZG9uYXRl)

I’ll close where I began.
In moments like these, trust doesn’t come from institutions — it comes from one another. From ordinary people choosing courage over comfort, truth over ease, and community over fear.
And ultimately, our confidence doesn’t rest in headlines or courts or outcomes still unseen. It rests in something firmer.
_“He who dwells in the shelter of the Most High will abide in the shadow of the Almighty. I will say to the Lord, ‘My refuge and my fortress, my God, in whom I trust.’”_ — Psalm 91:1–2
Keep the faith. Stay ready. Never quit. Ephesians 6 FTW!

Ever onward —
|
---
|
| **P.S.** I meant what I wrote: I believe deeply in the resolve of American patriots. History has shown what ordinary people can do when they are willing to roll up their sleeves and engage. But I am not naïve about the darkness of these days. That is why we are launching a new organization: **True the Vote NOW**. Its mission is to rally and organize citizens around election integrity — creating more capacity to coordinate, communicate, and act than True the Vote alone can provide. In the days ahead, togetherness will matter. Not just for election integrity, but beyond it. We are building that platform now. When we launch, we will let you know. And it will be soon. |

See this kid, Derek? [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/124919185/600115342/-1542703181?amounts=5,15,25,50,100,250,500&refcode=email_020726_bio&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTIvMS85MjU0MyIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI4MDQ3YzVlNi0zNTA0LWYxMTEtODMyZi0wMDBkM2ExZjBlNGMiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=hA61evGEYgTmXXTimvv0AyRCOQP84atK9gCHCPxr9II=) That’s me, Derek (headed to school at Ingram Elementary). I grew up right here in Western Pennsylvania, in Thornburg. As a kid, my family taught me the Western PA values we all know: hard work, service, and love of country. Those values shaped who I am, and they’ve guided me throughout my life. It’s these values that led me to step up and serve our country after the 9/11 attacks of my senior year of high school—entering the Naval Academy at just 17 years old. It’s these values that I lived by in the Navy, serving two deployments at sea and a tour on the ground in Iraq. Peter,
ICE has become a rogue, militarized police force operating with impunity, terrorizing immigrant communities, and violating the rights of American citizens.
Yet DHS refuses to hold them accountable. In fact, they're asking Congress to TRIPLE their budget.
Congress has the power to stop this. And I’m drawing a clear line: There will be NO new funding for DHS without real, enforceable accountability for ICE agents and plans for humane immigration reform.
I've introduced a comprehensive 10-point resolution to hold ICE accountable and restore the rule of law, and I will vote NO on any DHS funding bill that fails to meet these standards.
Here’s what my plan does:

✅ Repeal the multi-year $75 billion funding for ICE.

✅ Investigate and prosecute every single ICE agent who broke the law.
✅ End the Kavanaugh stops with racial profiling and the militarization of ICE.
✅ Codify a use-of-force standard so courts can enforce the law against rogue ICE agents.
✅ Tear down and replace ICE with an agency that has oversight.
✅ Prohibit masks and mandate body cameras and visible identification for immigration officers.
✅ Establish human rights standards at immigration detention facilities.
Let me be crystal clear: DHS will not get one more penny until ALL ten of these reforms are agreed to. I will not allow Congress to rubber-stamp funding for a "homeland security" agency that blatantly and unapologetically harms our people.

Peter,
When I first ran for office in 2018, I was a young candidate running to be a Cook County Commissioner--trying to break into a political system that wasn't built for people like me.
I was offered a contribution of $56,500 from a corporate PAC.
For a first-time candidate running for a county-level seat, that is a staggering amount of money. That is the type of check that can swing an election. It's the kind of money that propels careers and secures victories.
But I didn't even have to think about it.
I refused the check.
---
| | [](https://e96gjzhbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001d_Gqe3BSYq0J3XjwSb9vkiOjXVMkQgviw0UNjYsxZiE9mWiQugUOKFzywPBJ0MFLzG0hnwa9f5dimYcHa8Dmhg9chmER1SLOZ6ATYbOwTiG74Ftds0D02YKHyx27AWjlircjlpiAgO9gwDGD_C5ZooSjaH88cxyOz9mgJ36U4_MIj2S4fDdZ9vi3AQeCLgagaNrDSSuXDzwFYzubFv0aSKe8eYiySlKH&c=5V_tGKNuTh0PzFytyazcEJbJHFc83wfXq9pdQVwbQBHpy-NNoUogxA==&ch=DqlTtc_a2_FPLcw-Ki6HdJ8hJRgcHIc8-G3AQIUgjoKTLIPjmn72sw==)

| [](https://substack.com/redirect/564e0005-3b99-4ece-9930-f29eca50b5bb?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
A provocative idea is gaining traction among fiscal hawks and America-first economists: What if the U.S. government revalued its massive gold reserves at [market prices](https://substack.com/redirect/792f0062-3d58-44d9-8b40-b824f7722969?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), eliminated trillions in alleged waste and fraud, and radically simplified the tax code? Proponents argue this could sustain a lean $900 billion federal budget, preserve the world's largest military, and exempt all incomes under $500,000 from federal taxes. It's a bold vision that echoes recent DOGE initiatives and historical precedents, potentially reshaping America's economic landscape.

Let's break it down. The U.S. holds 261.5 million troy ounces of gold, [officially valued](https://substack.com/redirect/cdb7a312-e980-4052-94f5-97e79aa977da?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) at an archaic $42.22 per ounce - totaling just $11 billion on the balance sheet. But with gold trading at around $4,332 per ounce as of January 1, 2026, the real market value exceeds $1.13 trillion. Revaluing these reserves - a move proposed by figures like Sen. Cynthia Lummis and economist Judy Shelton - could inject over $1 trillion into the Treasury. This isn't printing money; it's marking assets to market, as done in past crises like the 1930s under FDR.
[Upgrade to paid](https://substack.com/redirect/2/eyJlIjoiaHR0cHM6Ly9oZWFydGxhbmRqb3VybmFsLnN1YnN0YWNrLmNvbS9zdWJzY3JpYmU_.0M60QEnpHF72U_bK3dTCRzZhLIlzCJeIqTg68dziALY?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget&utm_content=187203455)
How? The Treasury could issue gold certificates to the Federal Reserve, receiving dollars in return to retire debt. With national debt hovering near $35 trillion and annual interest payments topping $1 trillion, paying down even a portion could save $50 billion yearly in interest alone (assuming 5% rates). That's immediate fiscal breathing room, reducing the need for deficit spending and stabilizing the dollar without inflation spikes.

Now, pair this with eradicating "fraud" - a term popularized by Elon Musk's Department of Government Efficiency (DOGE). Musk has estimated government waste, improper payments, and outright fraud at a staggering $1.5 trillion annually, far exceeding DOGE's initial $214 billion in identified savings. Critics call it hyperbole but reports from Senate probes and OIG audits reveal billions squandered on redundant contracts, lease cancellations, and abuse in programs like Medicare and defense procurement. If DOGE delivers even half its promised cuts, federal spending could plummet from projected $7 trillion in FY2026 to a core $3-4 trillion - focused on essentials.

Under this scenario, income tax revenue - currently around $2.4 trillion - becomes redundant for most. Cumulative taxes from earners above $400,000 already hit $900 billion. Exempting those below $500,000 would yield roughly $850-900 billion from high earners alone, covering a stripped-down budget. Add corporate taxes ($500 billion), excises, and tariffs, and total revenues could align with needs.

Critically, this preserves U.S. military supremacy. The FY2026 defense bill authorizes over $900 billion - more than the next 10 nations combined. A $900 billion overall budget? Unrealistic today, but with gold revaluation offsetting debt and fraud cuts eliminating bloat, it's feasible to allocate the lion's share to defense while axing non-essentials like overlapping agencies and foreign aid.

Skeptics warn of market disruptions - gold prices could surge or dip on revaluation news - and one-time gains won't fix structural entitlements like Social Security ($1.5 trillion). Yet, precedents abound: Switzerland and Germany have revalued reserves without chaos, boosting credibility.
In a post-pandemic era of fiscal reckoning, this isn't fantasy - it's optimization. By floating gold and purging fraud, America could unleash growth, reward workers, and dominate globally. The question isn't if we can afford it; it's why we haven't already.

Simply put, the US collects $2.4T in income tax but spends $1.5T on fraud. If we didn't have to pay for fraud, only $900b would need to be collected. This means anyone with any less than 500k in income could pay *literally $0* in income tax. We don't need to raise taxes. we need to cut fraud.

| [](https://substack.com/redirect/045d34e2-c996-49a3-ba58-8d58eba3bec7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---

In 1913, zero American families paid income tax. In 2025, every family paid income tax, and about 2/3rds of it just covered fraud.

| [](https://substack.com/redirect/6f248d55-3719-4efa-8a08-45548f845109?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---

The largest source of federal revenue for most of U.S. history were tariffs on imported products and were essential to government funding pre 1913. Before the modern income tax (post-1913), the U.S. government funded itself primarily through these tarriffs. Now, given that for Fiscal Year (FY) 2025, U.S. tariff revenue saw a massive increase, with estimates ranging from roughly **$195 billion to over $200 billion** by year's end, we're fully funded.

This debut episode of _**Deep Dive with Ellie Leonard**_ set the tone for what this series will be: methodical, humane, and relentlessly evidence-driven. Ellie walked viewers through how citizen journalists are uncovering what institutions missed--or ignored--in the Epstein files, emphasizing receipts over rumors and collaboration over clout. Drawing on her background in transcribing major investigative journalism projects, Ellie explained how emails, financial records, and contemporaneous journals reveal patterns of abuse, institutional complicity, and deliberate inaction. The episode balanced hard investigative detail with ethical guardrails, stressing survivor protection, accuracy, and the risks journalists now face simply for telling documented truths.
* * *
### Key Takeaways
* **Citizen journalism matters:** Millions of independent eyes can uncover connections that official investigations overlook or suppress.
* **" Receipts" are everything:** Emails, contemporaneous journals, bank records, and file metadata matter more than speculation or viral claims.
* **Financial institutions enabled abuse:** Patterns in banking records--especially at JPMorgan--point to ignored red flags tied to sex trafficking.
* **Survivor credibility is reinforced by records:** Early journals and FBI reports validate accounts long dismissed or buried.
* **Disinformation is a real threat:** AI-generated images and misread documents can damage credibility and must be rigorously checked.
* **Journalists are being targeted:** Mishandled DOJ file releases and unredacted materials pose legal and personal risks to reporters and researchers.

subject: It’s retaliation

body:
When I demanded transparency and accountability for what’s happening in
Minnesota, the Department of Justice turned its attention to me.

That’s not a coincidence. It’s retaliation.

This is how authoritarian politics work: overwhelm your critics, weaponize
the justice system, and make the cost of speaking up so high that people
stop doing it.

I won’t stop, because Minnesota believes in the rule of law. We believe in
dignity. We believe real public safety comes from trust and cooperation —
not fear, chaos, or political theater.

But fighting back against this kind of retaliation is expensive by design.
And that’s why I’m asking for your help.

Peter,
Defend Our Courts has been sounding the alarm about Trump's plot to rig elections since our founding in Spring 2025.
In our first major race, the '25 Pennsylvania Supreme Court election, we laid out the stakes for Democrats: Trump is attempting to take control of PA state Supreme Court so that he will have control over the court with final say on election related matters in the most important swing state in America.
In short, we've been warning that Trump is trying to control how states run their elections by planting his loyalist judges on State Supreme Courts.
Our critics called us "alarmist." MAGA called us crazy.
But what Donald Trump announced proves without a doubt that the plot we have been warning about is very, very real:
---
| [](https://yfq78zhbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001nQ9xfLQsYZ_mNq9UP1vJ-oi0XKltIVeCqRJNayk-k1ODrtmh5chLUKEPxJnHlv4zScIpjgtoAIKbga_lZRuHh5C0BybEA_Xar4VVd3u5dNoX6chCfmaeNlX1PwIixHTkc_CFtwmwMo-aH9AAZIJvRmPM1RBvN7QSmT9lyzxVqZkiCH-kFg86Q8c7ypDKU9iYhXGP1kHB8veKZgosWSZpdjzBzpZK0XuVXUxsqQRYm28=&c=lSDzsyScT74udoebfz4huHobTMLJBPia-27GjxKOUmqN5YUVzLT1LQ==&ch=CiMFBpI0nNqAUH6GeP1N8u1wcA1hyTyUnUeImQQHOUvEC8slu3FOqw==)
---
Trump is now openly declaring his war on free and fair elections.
In the Constitution, it clearly outlines that state governments, not the federal government, have responsibility for how elections are administered. It's literally in the first Article of the Constitution.
And that means there's good news and bad news:
The good news: Trump's call to nationalize elections is so unconstitutional that even the MAGA controlled Supreme Court is unlikely to allow it.
The bad news: Now that Trump has publicly stated his end goal, MAGA's going to go nuclear to try and take control of state Supreme Courts across the country.
Defend Our Court's mission has never been more essential to preserving Democracy than it is now.
In 2026, there are state Supreme Court elections in several key swing states; Georgia, Michigan, and Wisconsin.
Last year, Defend Our Courts helped spearhead the defense of PA's state Supreme Court. And Democrats there didn't just win, they won massive 30+ point landslides. In Philadelphia where we concentrated the majority of our efforts, turnout surged by 34 percent. That was the largest increase in the state. And it made the difference.
Now we're taking our winning formula and our army of over 100k grassroots supporters to battle MAGA in GA, MI, and WI in 2026. With the national party stretched thin with House and Senate races, our role will be crucial in saving democracy.
[So we're asking you today: Can we count on you to pitch in $50, $25, or whatever you can spare to help us in the most crucial battle for Democracy yet and stop a Trump takeover of our elections?](https://yfq78zhbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001nQ9xfLQsYZ_mNq9UP1vJ-oi0XKltIVeCqRJNayk-k1ODrtmh5chLUKEPxJnHlv4zTso8ggld_ONrGImdsTpBzDzJp84mAGvF-fk2pe8PzfgoJwFZxL56oc_zwYks3cgJpeK-P1sHL8MJeDMLzy2GBMY31Y5_4c4q8sEkr5SdVVKLLce-HzVqCzXk8o476kLulKKEAE7pu84mBnWS0qugrATzcZvJVizOOLdtiVybOFFhqKyRlbxyPtBMyTR0pKc7&c=lSDzsyScT74udoebfz4huHobTMLJBPia-27GjxKOUmqN5YUVzLT1LQ==&ch=CiMFBpI0nNqAUH6GeP1N8u1wcA1hyTyUnUeImQQHOUvEC8slu3FOqw==)

* * *
* * *
In the spring of 2000, Michael Saylor watched his personal fortune evaporate in a single day. As co-founder and CEO of MicroStrategy, a business-intelligence software company he had built from scratch, Saylor saw the firm's stock plummet more than 60 percent after an SEC investigation revealed aggressive accounting practices that had inflated revenues during the dot-com frenzy.
The collapse erased roughly $6 billion in market value overnight, slashing Saylor's net worth from billions to a fraction of that. It was one of the starkest personal losses of the bubble era, a cautionary tale of over-leveraged ambition in a speculative mania.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/96aaef58-1e61-465f-b0ef-867eb78c7150?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Two and a half decades later, Saylor has reemerged as perhaps the most vocal and committed advocate for Bitcoin in the corporate world. No longer merely a software executive, he has repositioned his company--now rebranded as Strategy--as a de facto Bitcoin investment vehicle.
The strategy is audacious: use the company's equity and ability to take on debt to fund and amass Bitcoin at scale, treating it as a superior store of value to cash holdings amid inflation and currency debasement.
Saylor's thesis is straightforward and unyielding: Bitcoin is digital gold, scarce, decentralized, and destined to appreciate over the long term as fiat currencies erode. He has articulated this view in countless interviews, podcasts, and X posts, framing Bitcoin not as speculation but as an inevitable monetary evolution. One that Microstrategy would eventually emerge from as the apex predator.
[](https://substack.com/redirect/1648c907-1997-426d-8039-7b35c21fb3f4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
The pivot began in August 2020, when MicroStrategy announced its first major Bitcoin purchase: 21,454 coins for about $250 million. At the time, Bitcoin traded around $11,000, and the move was framed as a hedge against cash depreciation in a low-interest-rate world. What followed was relentless accumulation and the use of any and all means to achieve it. Through convertible debt offerings, at-the-market share sales, and other financing tools, the company bought during dips and rallies alike.
By early February 2026, Strategy held 713,502 Bitcoin, acquired at an average price of approximately $76,052 per coin, for a total cost basis of around $54.26 billion according to Strategy's own **[Strategy Bitcoin Purchases](https://substack.com/redirect/b738fe0d-0368-4f0f-8571-e3c82e344f99?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) **page. This represents more than 3.4 percent of Bitcoin's total fixed supply of 21 million coins according to **[The Block](https://substack.com/redirect/6780b0c9-71c5-4c2c-a654-d731c3d0d77d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).**
The mechanics of this buildup are as financial as they are ideological. Strategy's stock (**MSTR**) became a leveraged proxy for Bitcoin exposure. Investors buying shares effectively gained amplified upside (and downside) to Bitcoin's price movements, often at a premium to the underlying holdings. The company raised capital by issuing shares or convertible notes when the stock traded richly--sometimes at 1.5x or more the net asset value of its Bitcoin--and deployed those proceeds to buy more coins.
This created a feedback loop: rising Bitcoin prices boosted the stock, enabling more issuance and purchases, which in turn supported further price gains.
Central to this structure is the concept of a "liquidation price." Unlike margin traders who face forced sales at predefined thresholds if an investment goes bad, Strategy's Bitcoin is largely unencumbered--with no direct collateral calls on the holdings themselves. However, much of its debt is leveraged against the value of Strategy its self through convertible notes and share issuances, and aggressive dilution or covenant breaches of those could bring extreme pressure against the firm itself in "extreme" scenarios. The question yet to be answered is how "extreme" does a scenario have to be to be considered "extreme?"
Analysts have calculated "theoretical liquidation levels" based on debt divided by holdings; earlier estimates placed it far lower, around $20,000 per Bitcoin in prior years when debt was smaller relative to holdings according to **[21Shares Research](https://substack.com/redirect/b2e05bfd-00ac-427c-9b10-ffe74d5d3c85?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).**
The real risk is subtler: The best way for Saylor to combat a fall in Bitcoin prices would be to acquire more of them at a lower price, bringing his overall average cost down and spreading the investment across more coins.
However sustained low Bitcoin prices erode the stock's premium over net asset value, making new equity raises dilutive and/or unattractive to investors as their confidence in Saylor's overall thesis weakens. This would potentially limit Saylor's ability for further accumulation even if the price of Bitcoin would be considered by many "a bargain."
The recent downturn illustrates these dynamics vividly. After Bitcoin surged to highs well above $100,000 in late 2025, it has fallen sharply in early 2026, falling to a low of $60,020.52 and at the time of publishing sits at $70,394.27
This means that purely on the value of the Bitcoin held by Strategy, Saylor currently is underwater to the tune of more than $4 Billion. While shocking, this is however much better than it has been this week. At the market lows, the position was underwater by $11.43 Billion.
The company's stock has suffered accordingly, declining significantly from its peaks where it traded as high as $457.22 to a low of $102.50 as the premium evaporated and the market reassessed the risks of this leveraged bet.

Saylor remains defiant, continuing purchases even amid the pullback--most recently adding 855 Bitcoin for $75 million in late January to early February according to **[Bitcoin Magazine](https://substack.com/redirect/832948cc-b767-498e-bea2-d22dd372ad85?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).** Saylor views volatility as noise, insisting Bitcoin's long-term trajectory remains upward and that he will be proven correct on his thesis.

Yet the episode revives echoes of his dot-com past: bold conviction meeting market reality, with shareholders bearing the brunt of drawdowns.
What does this mean for the broader experiment in corporate Bitcoin adoption? Strategy's model has inspired imitators, but it also highlights the real world hazards of concentrating treasury strategy in a single volatile asset. If Bitcoin rebounds strongly, Saylor will be vindicated as a visionary who transformed a middling software firm into a crypto powerhouse.
If prolonged weakness persists, the structure could face strains--not from outright liquidation, but from eroded confidence, dilution fatigue, and questions about whether this is innovation or speculation dressed, ironically, as "Strategy."
In an era when traditional finance increasingly intersects with digital assets, Saylor's saga forces a reckoning: Can a public company responsibly treat Bitcoin as its core asset, or does the approach invite the same excesses that felled icons of past bubbles? The answer may not arrive for years, but the stakes--financial, philosophical, and systemic--are growing by the day.

If Bitcoin rebounds strongly, Saylor will be vindicated as a visionary who transformed a middling software firm into a crypto powerhouse. If prolonged weakness persists, the structure could face strains--not from outright liquidation, but from eroded confidence, dilution fatigue, and questions about whether this is innovation or speculation dressed, ironically, as "Strategy." In an era when traditional finance increasingly intersects with digital assets, Saylor's saga forces a reckoning: Can a public company responsibly treat Bitcoin as its core asset, or does the approach invite the same excesses that felled icons of past bubbles? The answer may not arrive for years, but the stakes--financial, philosophical, and systemic--are growing by the day. 3. **Phil is supported by the people of Colorado, not corporations, billionaires, and special interests.** He has never taken corporate PAC money–and is the only candidate committed to getting corporate money out of Colorado elections.

Dear Peter, A lot of things feel out of control right now. Costs keep rising, while paychecks don’t.
Families are watching ICE raids tear through their communities.
Basic freedoms feel more fragile than they used to.
And powerful institutions keep making decisions that ordinary people never asked for, and can’t undo. That’s why I’m reaching out today. [**If you’re able, chip in now to help United for Democracy get ready**** _before_****the next major Supreme Court decision drops, including a case that could further weaken the Voting Rights Act.**](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.iIBo0N5fSFzEFL40Tn-vtbMETCUYClkOrOh9-SNJfqsQNarR6PCR1lUtXpWTyhe63nGElJBICfxKS5eORA9eyhe3oXJINU5SF9rjvOxqd5VNypJayk9lbKr152j-5Zl-B2RGGk5BHNCovVoTm5FFJHDu0vBi6hPOWHywQ36l4O-zqdNnF_ghsKGnYw5SgjUt9We0V5oLxqLrD08fvCaQXJC6tX6LP9g2t3ukOZ-Nqew3wliEmt1OoGIh-4KEU8a27cj50KpJsaYRg6EyLcXGTHEVyxwxcyZgwusBaVTLL3AVJKsrz6Q6c53ajNgs8pNRjFL7CuEeCPCHDKq6P1MvFFkxlFjsQRwW5nnKMk6JrXlk-jvGLpeJrAcVp2L90EHuFQArebI7CtgSFRYpPF8U7g/4ny/Ka8_0xu9S_ORyS9dqji5qQ/h0/h001._owpssSk1NOZEFcsbCrg2mz4MqCZYpGHJw8BXAUysfw) This isn’t about panic. subject: ICE took his caregiver. Then he died.
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Able Dems PAC and not authorized by any candidate or candidate's committee
body:
| | | Friend, I am sick to my stomach. Last month, 30-year-old Wael Tarabishi died in a Texas ICU. He had Pompe disease and relied on his father, Maher, for every breath. ICE snatched Maher away months ago, ignoring every humanitarian plea. Wael died without his father’s hand to hold because this government decided that cruelty was more important than a disabled man’s life. **_This isn't just a Texas story. This is the blueprint for the cruel federal occupation of Minnesota._** Under "Operation Metro Surge," 3,000 armed agents are turning the Twin Cities into a war zone. We are seeing the same lethal disregard for disabled lives:
* Agents violently dragging Aliya Rahman, an autistic woman, from her car while she screamed about her disability.
* Special education students hiding in basements as agents batter down doors.
* The state-sanctioned killings of Renee Good and Alex Pretti by federal agents who refuse to answer to our laws.

They are hunting our neighbors, traumatizing our children, and letting our loved ones die alone. ENOUGH**.** **Able Dems is fighting to elect disabled leaders and allies who will stand in the gap, STOP ICE, and end this "federal invasion." We don't need "civility,"****_we need power._** [**Friend, chip in $25 right now. | | Charlie Kirk lived fast. And he lived loud.

He filled arenas. He lit a fire in the next generation on campus.

He confronted lies and spoke truth with boldness.

And he built a movement and a machine that few ever thought possible.

I saw it up close -- _Charlie moved at a pace most couldn 't keep up with. _

But in the middle of all the noise... he made a quiet decision that changed everything.

_**He started observing the Sabbath. **_

Not as a box to check. Not as a religious performance.

_But as an act of obedience. _

As a way of saying, **_" God, You are enough. And because You are enough, I need not carry the weight of a world that was never mine to hold." _**

Every week -- no matter what -- Charlie stopped.

He turned off the noise. He stepped away from the battlefield.

No email. No media. No work.

He gave his full attention fully to God, his wife Erika, and his children.

It was hard at first -- for someone who carried so much.

But over time, it changed him.

And before he was assassinated, he wrote a book about what he had learned...

Trust that rest is not weakness -- it's worship. In Stop, in the Name of God, you'll discover: 🔥 How Charlie reclaimed the Sabbath in a world built on burnout 🔥 What sacred rest gave back to him -- as a father, husband, and believer 🔥 Why he believed this message could spark revival in a restless generation Charlie wrote this book because he knew what it meant to nearly lose his peace -- and what it felt like to find it again. That's the heartbeat of his final message. Charlie Kirk didn't waste his time on earth. He left behind a family. He left behind a movement. And he left behind this truth... For anyone ready to step off the treadmill... and walk back toward what's eternal. Fellow Patriot, thank you -- in advance -- for helping reach the next generation with truth, faith, and moral courage. These are the very things Charlie gave his life for. May the message he left behind lead you -- just as it led him -- to a deeper trust in God... A stronger love for your family... And a renewed peace in your own soul. For Charlie, Justin Streiff Chief Operating Officer Turning Point USA P.S.Stop, in the Name of God is Charlie Kirk's final message -- written in obedience, shaped by Scripture, and grounded in trust in the Lord. 4940 East Beverly Road Phoenix, Arizona 85044

**This fight isn 't just about football.**

**Coach Tuberville was born in Camden, Arkansas, the third of three children of Olive and Charles Tuberville. College Football 's 2004 Coach of the Year and two-time SEC Coach of the Year, Tommy Tuberville is most often recognized for his success on the field. In 1989 Coach Tuberville met his future wife, Suzanne Fette, at the Sugar Bowl in New Orleans. They were married in 1991 and have two boys, Tucker and Troy, who continue to make their dad proud.

In 1998, Coach Tuberville was announced as the next head coach for the Auburn Tigers. body:
Corporate money doesn’t sit elections out, and neither can we.
# [](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/852?refcode=em20260207-1&t=1&akid=3125%2E587540%2E9nRncE)
Peter,
Every once in a while, we’ll hear people say things like, “Why donate to a candidate in a blue state? They’ll win anyway.” or “What’s the use in supporting progressives in ‘safe’ seats? It’s already in the bag.”
**But here’s the hard truth. No seat is ‘safe’ when corporate money is all that’s left to fill the gaps.** Even in deep blue districts, if progressives aren’t properly funded by grassroots supporters like you, then special interests will use that opportunity to take advantage of candidates who need to keep their campaigns afloat.
Then we’ll be left to wonder who those candidates will be accountable to. The short answer? _Not us._
That’s why this line of thinking keeps the influence of moneyed interests alive — and why it doesn’t work for the movement we’re trying to build.
When we fund progressive candidates, whether it be in a swing district or a deep blue stronghold, we ensure that our leaders are working for _us_ , _not mega donors or special interests._
It means that our leaders will keep their focus on delivering on the priorities that matter most to their communities, like affordability, healthcare, and workers’ rights, without being pulled in the wrong direction.

name: Jack Schlossberg
subject: I'm running for Congress!
body:
https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rtp-2025-jack?refcode=020726_1 [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rtp-2025-jack?refcode=020726_1]
It's official...
I'm running to represent NY-12 in Congress! This is the district where I was born and raised, and the place that five generations of my family have called home.
Hi Peter, I'm Jack Schlossberg, and my grandfather, President Kennedy, is my hero.
In high school, I spent hours watching his speeches. He taught us all that politics isn't about serving yourself — it's about serving others. And that's exactly why I'm running for Congress.
This isn't going to be your average campaign — we’re at the forefront of a movement backed by real people who are ready for a new generation of leadership. I won't be bought or intimidated. Instead, I'll be relying on folks like you. So, if you're willing to be one of the first donors to my campaign, will you split a donation between myself and Real Texas PAC right now? [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rtp-2025-jack?refcode=020726_1]
If you've saved your payment information with ActBlue Express, your donation to Jack Schlossberg and The Real Texas PAC will go through immediately:
DONATE $5 [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rtp-2025-jack?express_lane=true&refcode=020726_1&amount=5]
DONATE $10 [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rtp-2025-jack?express_lane=true&refcode=020726_1&amount=10]
DONATE $50 [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rtp-2025-jack?express_lane=true&refcode=020726_1&amount=50]
DONATE $100 [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rtp-2025-jack?express_lane=true&refcode=020726_1&amount=100]
DONATE $250 [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rtp-2025-jack?express_lane=true&refcode=020726_1&amount=250]
Other Amount [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rtp-2025-jack?refcode=020726_1&amount=25]
I've always been passionate about politics — you can probably gather as much if you've seen any of my social media posts :) I pride myself on my hot (correct!) takes. But public service has always been my driving force. I come from a long legacy of public service, from my great-great-grandparents to my mother, Caroline Kennedy.
I have big shoes to fill. I've known it all my life. But this is even bigger than living up to my family name. This is about serving the people of New York — the city that shaped me into the person I am today.
Right now, our country is in crisis. Donald Trump and his buddies (my cousin RFK Jr. — to name just one) are tanking the economy, attacking free speech, and sowing distrust in decades of scientific research.
We need to revive empathy and effort. I want to be excited and feel hopeful about our future, and I want my fellow New Yorkers to feel the same way. I believe in a politics that works for the people it was intended to serve, and I'm ready to fight for it.
And Peter, I happen to think caring is cool.
None of this will be easy. But in the words of my grandfather, I'm doing this "Not because it is easy but because it is hard."
Together, we can build a new Congress and a New York City that works for everyone. Will you join our movement today by splitting a donation of any amount between my campaign and Real Texas PAC ? [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rtp-2025-jack?refcode=020726_1]
Talk soon,
Jack

body:
| | | [](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/134?t=1&akid=7354%2E400544%2EdqaZq5)
---
[](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/4677?refcode=jtk256-fr-nd&t=2&akid=7354%2E400544%2EdqaZq5)
Hi friend, it's Deb Haaland. Did you hear the exciting news? **I have filed to be on the ballot to become New Mexico's next governor!**

I felt so honored to deliver ballot petitions signed by thousands of grassroots supporters across New Mexico. And I felt proud to wear my traditional ribbon skirt as I filed. When I wear traditional clothing — like my ribbon skirt or my mocs — I'm reminded of how powerful our clothing is to our shared heritage. **I rock my ribbon skirt to honor the people whose shoulders I stand on.**

In a minute, I'm going to share some of the other places I've **rocked my ribbon skirt and mocs.** [ _**But before I do, I have to ask:**_**_Will you please help us build on this winning momentum by giving $5 to my campaign right now?_**](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/5042?refcode=jtk256-fr-nd&t=3&akid=7354%2E400544%2EdqaZq5)
| | [Donate](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/4677?refcode=jtk256-fr-nd&t=4&akid=7354%2E400544%2EdqaZq5)
---
| | On the day I was sworn in as Secretary of the Interior, I decided to wear my white moccasins and a handmade ribbon skirt adorned with butterflies, stars, and corn. No matter where I go, I am a proud Pueblo woman first — including at the Department of the Interior.
---
[](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/4677?refcode=jtk256-fr-nd&t=5&akid=7354%2E400544%2EdqaZq5)
---
| | On the first day of the White House Tribal Nations Summit in 2021, I wore my beaded moccasins in solidarity with our Indigenous people across the country. I am incredibly grateful that together, our administration made extraordinary accomplishments for Indian Country — enduring progress that would make our ancestors proud.
---
[](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/4677?refcode=jtk256-fr-nd&t=6&akid=7354%2E400544%2EdqaZq5)
---
| | From my ancestral homelands here in New Mexico to the halls of Congress — and as I just filed my candidate petition to add my name to New Mexico's ballot for governor — I rock my ribbon skirt to honor my ancestors.
---
[](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/4677?refcode=jtk256-fr-nd&t=7&akid=7354%2E400544%2EdqaZq5)
---
Friend, history has shown us there’s nothing we can’t accomplish when we work together, which is why I’m counting on the support of people like you as we fight for a New Mexico that works for everyone.
I am so excited and thankful to everyone who helped me pass the first major hurdle in what will be an expensive and competitive race — but this race is just heating up, and we still have a long way to go till November.**I am ready to fight for an education that gives every child the chance to dream big and reach their full potential here in New Mexico. Give families a raise by increasing the minimum wage and the child tax credit. Protect affordable healthcare and expand access to treatment and recovery programs for those suffering from addiction.
**
**_[Please, friend: Will you chip in $5 right now so we can build a strong campaign capable of winning this race and making history again?](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/5042?refcode=jtk256-fr-nd&t=8&akid=7354%2E400544%2EdqaZq5)_**
| | [Donate](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/4677?refcode=jtk256-fr-nd&t=9&akid=7354%2E400544%2EdqaZq5)
---
I am so grateful for your support. Thank you for being by my side.

Be fierce,
Deb

Friend, February is Black History Month, which marks a time to honor and celebrate Black Americans and Black History. As a dad and former teacher, I want my kids to grow up knowing the stories that shape our home. That means celebrating Black artists and leaders who came from right here in Ohio. I think of Paul Laurence Dunbar, the Dayton poet whose words captured both pain and hope. I think of Toni Morrison, born in Lorain, whose novels opened the world’s eyes to the depths of Black life and imagination. I think of Sojourner Truth, whose powerful voice helped move our nation toward justice and whose story touched communities across Ohio. These stories matter because they remind us what’s possible when communities invest in each other. On Cincinnati’s city council, I worked to expand access to preschool because I saw firsthand how early opportunity changes a life. Honoring Black History Month means honoring that work — investing in education, uplifting local leaders, and making sure every child in our district can write their own story. That work has never been more important, and I’m honored to play a part in it each and every day in Congress. Thanks for all you do, and Happy Black History Month. In solidarity,
Greg Landsman 💙🙏

| **Friend —** **We have some good news... and some bad news.** ✅ **The good news:** Our JanePAC-endorsed climate champion Christian Menefee WON his race for Congress in Texas, _shrinking the GOP House majority to just one vote!_ Christian has spent years as Harris County Attorney suing fossil fuel giants and protecting long-ignored communities from pollution. Now he's in Washington, ready to continue that fight — and push back against where Donald Trump is taking this country. ❌ **The bad news:** Donald Trump is openly calling on Republicans to seize control of elections and “nationalize” voting in “at least 15 places” across the country. This is a blatantly unconstitutional power grab that would strip states of their authority and undermine free and fair elections. Let's be clear about what's happening: Trump sees the momentum we’re building ahead of the midterms, and he's running scared. So instead of letting voters choose their representatives at the ballot box, he's threatening to trample our freedoms and silence our voices by rigging the system in his favor. **That’s authoritarianism. name: Wes Climer
subject: Saving you money on a special election.
body:
| | | | | |
---
| | | | It’s always bothered me that when someone in elected office runs for another office and wins, their parting gift to their constituents is often a special election that leaves taxpayers on the hook for an expensive special election and unrepresented for a period of time.This has weighed on me since I announced I am running for Congress. I might not win, but what if I do?I’m tremendously grateful to the people of York County for allowing me to represent our community in the Senate, and the last thing I want to do is cost them hard-earned money and leave them without representation for any period of time.Existing laws governing special elections make it impossible for a legislator to resign in a way that would avoid costing taxpayers a lot of money and/or leaving them unrepresented. (It is possible to sequence a resignation in order to avoid either a primary, primary runoff, or a general election, but not all three.)An elections office official estimated that a special election in the district I represent would cost $75,000–$90,000 for each round of the election, bringing the total cost to somewhere between $150,000 and $270,000.Taxpayers shouldn’t have to shoulder that burden.In consultation with the Senate Clerk and Majority Leader Massey, I worked on an alternative: a concurrent resolution to modify the special election process (S.880).Under the terms of this resolution, if a legislator irrevocably resigns by March 1, the special election to replace him would be concurrent to the existing election schedule — same filing period, same primary election, same primary runoff, same general election. And, importantly, an irrevocable resignation can be dated into the future, meaning a legislator can continue to represent his constituents while the election to replace him transpires.This should be permanent law — it would save taxpayers millions of dollars and greatly increase voter participation — but the process of changing permanent law would take longer than is feasible for this upcoming election. So, for now, a resolution like S.880 is the only viable option.This resolution has passed in the Senate and is pending consideration in the House. If the House chooses to pass it and Governor McMaster signs it, I will irrevocably resign as of November 2, 2026 — the day before the general election.This will allow my constituents to avoid going unrepresented in the Senate for a single day and save them $150,000–$270,000.This is America. Nobody is entitled to anything in politics or public service. Every single vote has to be earned. I’m working hard to earn the trust and confidence of the people of the Fifth Congressional District and fully appreciate that they have a range of choices.I think my principled conservatism stands pretty good odds and I’m deeply grateful for the outpouring of support I’ve received so far, but I might not be the one they ultimately choose to represent them in Congress.Nevertheless, resigning under the terms of this resolution is the only path I could find that would satisfy my responsibility to act in my constituents’ best interest, regardless of how the Congressional election goes or how it might affect me personally.
Thank you for letting me serve you,Wes Climer

name: Gina Hinojosa
subject: Abbott sold out our kids
body:
Abbott put a price tag on our kids’ education and is handing the bill to Texas families.
# [](https://ginafortexas.com/?refcode=em_ms_gh_header)[](https://ginafortexas.com/?refcode=em_ms_gh_header)
Peter,
One of Greg Abbott’s biggest grifts yet is officially underway, and our public schools are squarely in the line of fire.
With applications now open, his school voucher scheme is moving from plan to reality, and he expects hardworking Texas families to foot the bill.
Let’s be clear: This is a reckless, exclusionary scam that takes public money out of our neighborhood schools and hands it to private institutions that can pick and choose who they let in, and who they leave behind.
I’m tired of the political tricks, Peter, and I know you are too. I won’t allow Abbott to drain our neighborhood schools and take opportunity out of the hands of 5.5 million Texas public school kids.
And I know what’s at stake because this fight is personal for me. I first ran for office when my son’s public school was threatened with closure, so I’ve seen up close how much our communities rely on strong neighborhood schools, and how devastating it is when politicians treat them as disposable.
Our public schools need investment and support, not to be gutted by Abbott so that he can line the pockets of his billionaire donors.
But here’s the good news, Peter: _We can stop him._
I’ve beat Abbott on this issue before. By standing with parents, educators, and communities who refuse to let _anyone_ gamble with their kids’ futures. When I’m governor, we’ll shut down this attack on our neighborhood schools and get back to putting our kids first. But to get there, I need you with me in this fight.
**[If you’re able, chip in $5 today to end the voucher grift and send Abbott a message loud and clear: we won’t allow him to cash in on our kids.](https://act.ginafortexas.com/go/625?c0=em_ms_gh_20260207_1_vouchers.M1MCL3&refcode=em20260207-545&amount=5&t=1&akid=545%2E299639%2Eeu7g7R)**

Thank you for standing with me in this fight.
With gratitude,
Gina

| | Peter,
---
| | Charlie Kirk lived fast. And he lived loud.

He filled arenas. He lit a fire in the next generation on campus.

He confronted lies and spoke truth with boldness.

And he built a movement and a machine that few ever thought possible.

I saw it up close -- _Charlie moved at a pace most couldn 't keep up with. _

But in the middle of all the noise... he made a quiet decision that changed everything.

_**He started observing the Sabbath. **_

Not as a box to check. Not as a religious performance.

_But as an act of obedience. _

As a way of saying, **_" God, You are enough. And because You are enough, I need not carry the weight of a world that was never mine to hold." _**

Every week -- no matter what -- Charlie stopped.

He turned off the noise. He stepped away from the battlefield.

No email. No media. No work.

He gave his full attention fully to God, his wife Erika, and his children.

It was hard at first -- for someone who carried so much.

But over time, it changed him.

And before he was assassinated, he wrote a book about what he had learned...

clean_body: | | | | | Peter, | | Charlie Kirk lived fast. And he lived loud. He filled arenas. He lit a fire in the next generation on campus. He confronted lies and spoke truth with boldness. And he built a movement and a machine that few ever thought possible. I saw it up close -- Charlie moved at a pace most couldn 't keep up with. But in the middle of all the noise... he made a quiet decision that changed everything. He started observing the Sabbath. Not as a box to check. Not as a religious performance. But as an act of obedience. As a way of saying, " God, You are enough. And because You are enough, I need not carry the weight of a world that was never mine to hold." Every week -- no matter what -- Charlie stopped. He turned off the noise. He stepped away from the battlefield. No email. No media. No work. He gave his full attention fully to God, his wife Erika, and his children. It was hard at first -- for someone who carried so much. But over time, it changed him. And before he was assassinated, he wrote a book about what he had learned... This was Charlie's final message. His final act of trust. A book not about politics... but about peace. It 's called: Stop, in the Name of God. Peter, like I mentioned, this isn't a political book. It's not a culture war manifesto. It's a call to stop. To rest. To breathe. To return to God. Because Charlie believed America hadn 't just forgotten truth... It had forgotten trust. Trust that the world keeps spinning when you step away. Trust that God is in control. Trust that rest is not weakness -- it's worship. In Stop, in the Name of God, you'll discover: 🔥 How Charlie reclaimed the Sabbath in a world built on burnout 🔥 What sacred rest gave back to him -- as a father, husband, and believer 🔥 Why he believed this message could spark revival in a restless generation Charlie wrote this book because he knew what it meant to nearly lose his peace -- and what it felt like to find it again. That's the heartbeat of his final message. Charlie Kirk didn't waste his time on earth. He left behind a family. He left behind a movement. And he left behind this truth... For anyone ready to step off the treadmill... and walk back toward what's eternal. Peter, thank you -- in advance -- for helping reach the next generation with truth, faith, and moral courage. These are the very things Charlie gave his life for. May the message he left behind lead you -- just as it led him -- to a deeper trust in God... A stronger love for your family... And a renewed peace in your own soul. For Charlie, Justin Streiff Chief Operating Officer Turning Point USA P.S.Stop, in the Name of God is Charlie Kirk's final message -- written in obedience, shaped by Scripture, and grounded in trust in the Lord. 4940 East Beverly Road Phoenix, Arizona 85044

name: Josh Shapiro
subject: We’ve gotten a hell of a lot done, Derek. But there’s more to do.
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY SHAPIRO FOR PENNSYLVANIA
body:
Our kids are getting a better quality education. Our workers have more opportunities to chart their own course.

Earlier this week, I had the privilege of delivering my fourth budget address as Governor — where I laid out my vision to build on all the progress we’ve made together. [_**I’ll tell you more in a second — but the truth is this: In order to build a stronger, more affordable, more prosperous Pennsylvania for years in the future, we need to win the next election, Derek. And I need this team in my corner to do it. Please, can you chip in just a few dollars to support our movement here in Pennsylvania?**_](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/124935466/600165716/-1395620021?refcode=email_020726_budget&amounts=10,25,50,100,250,500,1000&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMDYvMS84NTY5MyIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI2OTllMzU4NS01MjA0LWYxMTEtODMyZi0wMDBkM2ExZjBlNGMiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=fw4nA8Mej47Dlzl70ssecsX3PtHTMUUKbAVtseTqIwA=) Derek, I know government can be a force for good in people’s lives. I know because I’ve seen it over the past three years. Our kids are getting a better quality education. Our workers have more opportunities to chart their own course. Our economy is growing, and our communities are safer. **We’ve done that work, together.** And Derek, we’ve done it in a way that shows we respect all people — no matter what you look like, where you come from, who you love, or who you pray to, or choose not to pray to. Yes, we’ve made great strides over the last three years. But we’ve got a lot more to do. That’s why my budget directs $565 million more to the schools that need it most through the new adequacy formula we created together. I’m calling for sustainable, recurring funding for mass transit — so every Pennsylvanian has a way to get to work, go to school, and travel wherever they need to go safely and reliably. I’m calling on the legislature to double down on our work expanding the supply of child care workers across the Commonwealth. **And yes, I’m calling on the Pennsylvania Legislature to raise the minimum wage to $15 an hour.** At a time when dysfunction and chaos define our federal government, Pennsylvania is showing the nation that we can be a model for steady progress when we come together, treat others with respect, and find ways to extend a helping hand to our neighbors. **That’s what I’ve done for over three years as your Governor — and it’s what I’ll continue to do here in Pennsylvania.** [_**Pennsylvania is on the rise — and I’m determined to keep it that way, Derek. By bringing down costs and protecting our most fundamental freedoms. ---|---|---
Most Republican Town Committees in Connecticut have given up on congressional elections.
The reasons are familiar. Unlike state legislative races, which are publicly funded, congressional elections are not and are often underfunded. After years without a Republican Congressman or U.S. Senator--and losses in all five congressional districts--a sense of defeat has taken hold.
But that resignation comes at a real cost. Congressional representation matters deeply to Connecticut, and abandoning federal races has consequences that affect everyday life across the state.
**Why Members of Congress Matter in Connecticut**
**Energy: Cost, Reliability, and Economic Survival**
Federal law determines what energy sources we use, how electricity is generated, and how much consumers pay. The United States is approaching a national electricity crisis, driven by the rapid expansion of data centers, AI computing, and electrification mandates.
Connecticut is a double loser:
* We already have some of the highest electricity costs in the country
* Energy-intensive industries and the jobs they create will not locate here
* Our aging electric grid faces real risks of shortages and brownouts

The most cost-effective and cleanest fossil fuel is natural gas, with clean coal also playing a role. Connecticut does not produce natural gas and must import it by pipeline.
There is abundant natural gas in Pennsylvania, but under current federal law, New York's governor has veto authority over new or expanded pipelines that could bring that gas to Connecticut.
Connecticut's congressional delegation has taken no serious action to remove or reform this veto power. Instead, they promote offshore wind--one of the most expensive and unreliable methods of electricity generation.
Removing this veto power is essential to Connecticut's economic survival. Solar and wind are intermittent and cannot meet rising demand on their own.
**Nuclear Energy**
Nuclear power is clean, reliable, and carbon-free. Connecticut's Millstone plants are aging, yet outdated federal regulations make building new nuclear facilities slow and prohibitively expensive.
Federal law must be modernized to expedite small modular and next-generation nuclear reactors, which could provide safe, affordable, long-term power. Without Republicans in Congress, this will not happen.
**Transportation: I-95 Is a Federal Failure**
Interstate 95 in Fairfield County is one of the most congested highways in the nation. Roughly 80% of funding to expand and modernize I-95 comes from the federal government.
Yet Connecticut's congressional delegation has consistently resisted highway expansion in favor of forcing commuters into mass transit. In Fairfield County, that means relying on one rail line with two northbound spurs--an unrealistic alternative for most residents.
Better highways would:
* Reduce commute times
* Lower fuel consumption
* Improve productivity
* Increase quality of life

Traffic congestion is a hidden tax on time, health, and economic output. When Washington ignores the problem, nothing improves. Every day spent stuck on I-95 is a reminder that federal representation matters.
**Healthcare: Government Is Driving the Crisis**
Healthcare costs continue to rise faster than inflation while physician burnout increases and patient satisfaction declines.
The fundamental problem is too much government regulation and too little competition. A full federal takeover of healthcare would require trillions in new entitlements and would worsen waste, inefficiency, and access problems.
Many Democrats support Medicare for All. The predictable outcome would be an expansion of concierge medicine for the wealthy and greater healthcare disparities for everyone else.
When taxes and regulation rise too high, incentives to work, innovate, and provide care disappear.
**Housing Costs: Congress Shapes Affordability**
Mortgage interest rates are driven by federal spending, inflation, and economic policy--areas where Congress has enormous influence.
I have proposed a Modern Homestead Act to help middle- and working-class families become homeowners by rehabilitating cities, creating new paths to ownership, and allowing families to build equity.
Combined with school choice and voucher systems, this approach would help families build wealth without sacrificing their children's education.
**Job Training: A Missed Federal Opportunity**
Congress can help finance training programs for construction trades, mechanics, healthcare professionals, and other skilled labor. These are real jobs with real pay that strengthen Connecticut's economy and reduce dependency on government assistance.
**Foreign Policy: Why It Matters at Home**
Foreign policy affects Connecticut residents directly--through energy prices, supply chains, national security, and immigration pressures. Weak leadership abroad creates instability that comes home in the form of higher costs and greater risk.
Congress controls sanctions, trade policy, military funding, and foreign aid. Serious representation in Washington is essential to restoring strength, deterrence, and realism in U.S. foreign policy.
**The Hard Truth Connecticut Republicans Need to Hear**
The Goldstein Team has been going to Washington without holding office--meeting with policymakers, advocates, and national leaders--raising Connecticut issues on energy, infrastructure, housing, healthcare, and workforce policy.
What we have seen should be a wake-up call:
* There is real interest in Connecticut
* There is openness to federal reforms that would benefit this state
* There is frustration in Washington that Connecticut never shows up organized or unified

In fact, there is more excitement for Connecticut solutions outside Connecticut than among Republicans inside the state.
Washington responds to organized constituencies.
When Connecticut shows no interest, it gets ignored.
**RTCs Are the Missing Link**
Republican Town Committees are the only institutions close enough to voters to connect local pain to federal power.
When Washington sees:
* Engaged RTCs
* Consistent messaging from towns
* Grassroots validation behind federal priorities

Doors open. Conversations change. Momentum builds.
The Goldstein Team already has national relationships and credibility.
What has been missing is local activation from Connecticut itself.
**Call to Action**
If you are an RTC chair, officer, or active member:
* Reach out to us
* Bring your town's federal issues forward
* Engage in coordinated federal advocacy
* Help show that Connecticut Republicans are awake, organized, and serious

This is not about endorsements.
It is not about money.
It is not about ego.
It is about representation.
The Goldstein Team is already doing the work in Washington.
Now Connecticut Republicans must meet the moment.
**Final Thought: A Wake-Up Call**
Other states fight for their interests every day.
Connecticut waits--and pays the price.
If Republican Town Committees stay on the sidelines, nothing changes.
If they engage--even imperfectly--everything starts to move.
Federal representation starts town by town.
It starts with RTCs.
It starts now.

Arizona Republicans are pushing bills to force hospitals to ask patients about their immigration status. This weaponizes healthcare — and we're fighting back. |
# [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/124935505/600165979/-1397648958?refcode=AU_AZD_FR_GEN_GEN_AC_20260207_PM1_V1_S1&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMjUvMS8xMDU1MTYiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiMmY1YjU0MzItNTQwNC1mMTExLTgzMmYtMDAwZDNhMWYwZTRjIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=J6MelvjC_P0EjOA2XROMiby8OPg-eHnm_uq__iOsvtk=)
---
Team, The Arizona state legislative session began on January 12th, and Republicans immediately reintroduced bills requiring hospitals to collect patient immigration data. **SB 1051 and HB 2689:**
* Force any hospital accepting AHCCCS (Medicaid) to ask patients during intake whether they're a U.S. citizen, lawfully present, or undocumented
* Sponsored by Senator Wendy Rogers and Representative Ralph Heap
* Passed through committees on party-line votes in late January
* Governor Katie Hobbs vetoed a similar version last session and is expected to veto these, too

Republicans call these "transparency measures" to calculate healthcare costs for undocumented immigrants. Democrats call it what it is: weaponizing healthcare to scare people away from emergency rooms for fear of deportation. The bills claim responding is voluntary and won't affect care. But when people are afraid to seek medical treatment because they'll be asked about immigration status, that's not voluntary — that's intimidation. And aggregated data can still be used to target facilities or communities for ICE enforcement. **[Chip in to support Democrats fighting back against Republicans weaponizing healthcare.](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/124935506/600165980/1861397980?contactdata=hSvtiDuOb9jxAayY2394ZaQCMufBd2pA6Dw+cOJ0t5BCZ0AjAFGgd0Nhc0QTWuRzWxBongLpRH2cKAaznPuQgM8eW3dmBpgXYtl/JotVONBtZLM8vEzG3w2YFelc43BEK3r3Zte3+W6Ur8hCjTIRrQ==&refcode=AU_AZD_FR_GEN_GEN_AC_20260207_PM1_V1_S1&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMjUvMS8xMDU1MTYiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiMmY1YjU0MzItNTQwNC1mMTExLTgzMmYtMDAwZDNhMWYwZTRjIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=J6MelvjC_P0EjOA2XROMiby8OPg-eHnm_uq__iOsvtk=)** | [CHIP IN NOW](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/124935507/600165981/1861397980?contactdata=hSvtiDuOb9jxAayY2394ZaQCMufBd2pA6Dw+cOJ0t5BCZ0AjAFGgd0Nhc0QTWuRzWxBongLpRH2cKAaznPuQgM8eW3dmBpgXYtl/JotVONBtZLM8vEzG3w2YFelc43BEK3r3Zte3+W6Ur8hCjTIRrQ==&refcode=AU_AZD_FR_GEN_GEN_AC_20260207_PM1_V1_S1&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMjUvMS8xMDU1MTYiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiMmY1YjU0MzItNTQwNC1mMTExLTgzMmYtMDAwZDNhMWYwZTRjIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=J6MelvjC_P0EjOA2XROMiby8OPg-eHnm_uq__iOsvtk=)

name: Dr. Kristin Hook
subject: Ten More Days Til Early Voting!
body:
| | | | | [|
---](https://drkristinhook.us13.list-manage.com/track/click?u=fd888d2bb4a2d4cad917af4b9&id=8c0d56f688&e=395a33a3d2)
| | | | | | Hi –
It’s hard to believe we are so close the March 3rd primary and start of early voting on February 17th!
**Are you**[**fired up and ready to go**](https://drkristinhook.us13.list-manage.com/track/click?u=fd888d2bb4a2d4cad917af4b9&id=95d57da14c&e=395a33a3d2)**?** I know I am!
A week ago, [we saw yet another Democratic victory and stunning upset in a deep-red district](https://drkristinhook.us13.list-manage.com/track/click?u=fd888d2bb4a2d4cad917af4b9&id=9a78b5d350&e=395a33a3d2) – this time right here in TEXAS!
---
[|
---](https://drkristinhook.us13.list-manage.com/track/click?u=fd888d2bb4a2d4cad917af4b9&id=adefcf9666&e=395a33a3d2)
| |
Taylor Rehmet defeated a MAGA opponent and won a district that [Republicans have carried by ~19 points](https://drkristinhook.us13.list-manage.com/track/click?u=fd888d2bb4a2d4cad917af4b9&id=d91234fd50&e=395a33a3d2) in 44 state and federal races since 2018. [His victory was in no small part due to support from Hispanic voters](https://drkristinhook.us13.list-manage.com/track/click?u=fd888d2bb4a2d4cad917af4b9&id=2fc1769211&e=395a33a3d2) who are fed up with racial profiling, mass deportations, and ICE’s state-sanctioned violence terrorizing our communities.

body:
|
# [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/124936767/600169839/336227065?refcode=em-header&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMzAvMS85MDE1MyIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJlZDI2NTQ4Yy01NzA0LWYxMTEtODMyZi0wMDBkM2ExZjBlNGMiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=5b1op11PMCnpSYDcmi6mNDEtBHBYQ8yTajQ2iA_b_-A=)
Peter,

Last year, the Trump Administration proposed deep cuts to NASA in the largest-scale attack on the agency in its history.

**This is personal to me -- I served as NASA Chief of Staff under President Obama.**
[](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/124936768/600169840/-635348808?refcode=em-2.7.26-all-b&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMzAvMS85MDE1MyIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJlZDI2NTQ4Yy01NzA0LWYxMTEtODMyZi0wMDBkM2ExZjBlNGMiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=5b1op11PMCnpSYDcmi6mNDEtBHBYQ8yTajQ2iA_b_-A=&emci=e426548c-5704-f111-832f-000d3a1f0e4c&emdi=ed26548c-5704-f111-832f-000d3a1f0e4c&ceid=36198509)
I’m proud that, working with my colleagues, Congress rejected the cuts to NASA. But there is still a whole lot of work left to be done. As the vice-ranking member for the Science Committee, I’m now working to pass the NASA Authorization Act, which governs all of NASA’s activities.

David Steiner, a former CEO of the nation’s largest waste management company who currently serves on the FedEx board of directors, has taken over control of the U.S. Postal Service, becoming the nation’s 76th postmaster general.
Steiner’s appointment brought heightened concerns from postal unions over possible efforts to privatize the USPS, which the Trump administration has advocated for. name: Tim Walz
subject: Three things I know for sure
disclaimer_text: paid for by Walz for Governor
body:
I’m counting on our supporters to have our backs.
#
Peter,
There’s a lot happening in Minnesota right now, and a lot of moving pieces at play. But here are three things I know for sure:
1) **Minnesota is being targeted by the Trump administration** in a campaign of political retribution. They aren’t interested in what’s best for Minnesota. Instead, they’re trying to make an example out of us.
2) **Communities across our state are uniting to get through this together** — and I couldn’t be more proud of them. Minnesotans are pulling through, _like we always do._
3) **Our legal costs are mounting.** The reality is, the Department of Justice’s bogus investigation could very well cost us millions of dollars when all is said and done.
I’m counting on our allies in every part of the country to step up and have our backs. This is one of the toughest fights I’ve faced in my decades of public service, so I’m asking for your support as I continue to stand up for Minnesota in the courts and on the streets.
**[So](https://act.timwalz.com/go/73?c0=em_tw_20260207.r2BeBT&amount=5&refcode=em20260207-464&t=1&akid=464%2E34582%2ENcx5Zk)****[Peter, will you pitch $5 to our Legal Defense Fund? Your contribution will go toward legal fees as I continue to do my job and defend the people of Minnesota.](https://act.timwalz.com/go/73?c0=em_tw_20260207.r2BeBT&amount=5&refcode=em20260207-464&t=2&akid=464%2E34582%2ENcx5Zk)**

Thank you,
Tim
