name: Squad Victory HQ
subject: Know your rights, Peter
body:
[ https://act.squadvictoryfund.com/go/18910?refcode=em20260207-1911-foote&t=1001&akid=1911%2E342411%2E4njeQc ]Squad Victory Fund

Peter,

Across the country, ICE continues to tear families apart, criminalize
immigrants, and operate with next to no accountability. It’s traumatic and
has cost people their lives.

And yet, in the face of recent tragedies, we’re seeing incredible
strength.

In Minnesota, people are rising together — peacefully, courageously — to
take a stand after ICE shot and killed Renee Good, Alex Pretti, and Keith
Porter. And across the country, we’re seeing neighbors, organizers, and
people showing up to protect one another, document abuses, and demand
better.

That kind of collective action matters. It’s proof that even when systems
fail us, people don’t. And this is how change is made.

That’s why we’re uplifting opportunities to take action that actually keep
people safe and build long-term power.

One of those opportunities is through the National Lawyers Guild (NLG).
For decades, the NLG has stood alongside movements for justice providing
Know Your Rights trainings and critical tools that help people protest,
organize, and protect themselves when law enforcement or federal agencies
are involved. Their work helps ensure that people can stand up for their
communities without standing alone.

If you’re asking, “What can I do right now?” — this is one answer.

1. [ https://act.squadvictoryfund.com/go/20216?t=1002&akid=1911%2E342411%2E4njeQc ]Get involved with the National Lawyers Guild. Take a Know Your
Rights training and help bring legal protections to the people who
need them most.
2. [ https://act.squadvictoryfund.com/signup/jan-2026-abolish-ice/?source=em20260207-1911&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=1003&akid=1911%2E342411%2E4njeQc ]Sign our petition to abolish ICE and get them off our streets
before more lives are lost.

We believe that real change only comes when ordinary people organize,
speak out, and act together. Let’s meet this moment with the collective
power it demands.

Thank you,

Squad Victory HQ

P.S. If you’re able, [ https://act.squadvictoryfund.com/go/19213?c0=svfem-20260207-movement.zRIApU&refcode=em20260207-1911&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=1004&akid=1911%2E342411%2E4njeQc ]please consider making a $3
contribution to the Squad Victory Fund today to keep up the fight for
bold, progressive change and justice on all fronts.

[ ](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/124937277/600171412/-629675555?refcode=email-header&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNTkvMS8xMDY3MjEiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiOTdiNmU1YWEtNTgwNC1mMTExLTgzMmYtMDAwZDNhMWYwZTRjIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=ykpPokskq7StfX9oCbpKdykmton1DDU5b_S1XhOzONs=) Since taking full control of our federal government, my Republican colleagues have been dodging town halls, hiding from their constituents, and refusing to take accountability for their failed leadership. _It’s wrong._ I’ve known from the start that my job as a representative is to show up, listen, and learn how to best support Oregonians. That's why I've made it a top priority to ensure everyone in OR-05 can make their voices heard. In 2025, I hosted 21 town halls and met with 94,000 Oregonians to understand how I can better represent our communities in Washington. **And I’m continuing to meet face-to-face with Oregonians in 2026.** Already this year, we’ve hosted three town halls in Deschutes, Clackamas, and Linn Counties — and there’s plenty more to come! My extreme opponent would be more of the same: a rubber stamp on the Trump agenda. Peter, this is a time to stand up and fight for our country’s future. I am ready. But I can’t stand alone. Thanks, Roy Paid for by State Democrats Committee (StateDemocrats.com). Not authorized by any federal candidate or candidate committee.

body:
| Team,

The Voter Protection Project and I agree that we need to abolish ICE. The violence and mayhem they are committing around the country show that ICE is beyond repair. But here's the thing: abolishing ICE is not enough. Democrats need an actual plan for what’s next to fix our broken immigration system.

Donald Trump has turned ICE into his own personal enforcers of our broken and racist immigration system. The entire machine needs to be dismantled and rebuilt, with consequences for those who have violated Americans’ rights while hiding behind a mask.

Here's what we need to do:
1\. Abolish ICE
2\. Prosecute the ICE and CBP officers who murdered American citizens and violated constitutional rights
3\. Build a comprehensive and humane immigration system that incentivizes people to come here legally instead of illegally, provides a clear pathway to citizenship, and is supported by an enforcement system that reflects American values in every action and policy.

Throughout four tours in Iraq, team, I saw first-hand the chaos that comes from bringing down violent enforcers without a plan for what comes next. We need to heed those lessons right now, and not only abolish ICE, but have an immediate plan of action to fix our broken immigration system.

Derek, it's Alex Vindman.
Today marks 6 years since Donald Trump fired me after I blew the whistle on his not-so-perfect phone call with Ukraine.
I’ve risked everything because I refuse to bow down to a wannabe tyrant. I refuse to start now.
Donald Trump and his allies may try to attack me, but I’m not backing down from the fight against chaos and corruption. That’s why I am running for the United States Senate in Trump’s backyard — and why I am humbly asking:
**[Will you please rush a donation to my campaign for Senate and Adam Schiff to help us check Trump’s power? Your donations add up quickly when everyone is chipping in what they can.](https://act.adamschiff.com/go/1014?c0=abs-em-alexvindman26.LuyiPk&refcode=AU_ABS_FR_TAN_GEN_AC90_20260207_AM1_V1_S1&t=4&akid=9513%2E5257348%2EuNhTrM)**

---

When I joined the Army, I took an oath to defend our nation and its values. I served at the Pentagon under presidents from both parties, putting our nation’s safety before politics.
The decision to report that call wasn’t for political gain. It was to protect our democracy. I believe I served my nation by helping expose corruption by the chief executive, and I would do it again today.
The reality is, we are still in the fight for the soul of our country. We need leaders who have the courage to take on the corruption and lower costs for our families in the Senate.
I know we can defeat Donald Trump’s handpicked candidate and win this race...but I can’t do it without you.

body:
Affordable Care Act insurance signups are down by hundreds of thousands compared to last year, and counting. Why? Because the monthly premiums are skyrocketing. | | | [](http://links.matsuiforcongress.com/s/c/bPgwxCWsgurYeMLYl-XXek27yj_LLOUwlUc4KauT6aLn6iL1BrS3o5JKNwqtk1Cg3Yv_MbuyIGQ0LX2Gx7aZEZAPeRcV-27oHkQEXGuRLmZMpyhm0hPmS80aWqTn7LsytOyJ6j3pwH9tiPUfqTyB9wsmokBAD70TcOf2QHm3n_DjX3Wa_3Im_SssWBaGgEryvWVmJX18fKu9cNwSyRURAqRfTFJr8lyRzsMRnX1Z84C1qhP6d6oS8Qk0mAiDNcRmy4FUyEF936hiTnB5KvRx6oHykkZdKCXhEqdCOalsSCpoYLlDZCnigCYTj3vbc0AIoMDDkrzItaWCkFGt762nzx2y1Gig7eV172UBNPFd12H5d-V-2ebKll3xc64_hMeT278XiPmYJak8co-5Il-2oba39ZEUl5QtfgrNEpBJhc-xgqRByFQa-LsrsEQKcQTg46aUyZEhKJTSDOjYzj2HV5vBJNviciT-k7ZCCLpj6AQg-hixRaFCITbNb_n-2KJm190G4EAWfszDFBn3AE4EEwg3Z66t17OtwVuq6NHFazL3GtvKpeaz15a4hl3VubgCUE8nAFMFL2lOlW2aK41_4om3JctPi0usLhQnzifV6wpNgxIWZ8-_a6xd5heVSi-uKbKFGiZmGCeJR6cY4sJWEGerh4FH_bna9HNaKaXK4RM7GE2qruTfc77sVVLau_vcQWdKUCBWZNIbvumSlniPJMXz80EtBk7mSUEadkH0v5kDTfeqmJNeXV-hTZBxv9K7o8Pjt5YvuUHmGSkwKg_hiGOm9JJAkXWuPrFOUZWE_GR1fIFNpAv0pnZPDNoYioFNB4uKqaWCYzwYXD2q2GphF_1gp_xbN4Kkc72MeLvO4CDWtJNH2RyVVgI1p2zRg5wPT8G4Pcf7tyGVmw_QPw/tyRmw2hyqMTTYulGWeu21j0jCwUZOJ7z/17)
Friends, Affordable Care Act insurance signups are down by hundreds of thousands compared to last year, and counting. Why? Because **the monthly premiums are skyrocketing.** Americans all over our country are hoping they don’t have any health issues this year, **because they can’t afford the bill.** Healthcare access is a fundamental right—not a luxury. No family should have to choose between groceries for the week and going to the doctor. As we dive in to the year of the midterm elections, I am asking for something deeply important. And no, it’s not money.

Today, I am asking for your direct input.

**Will you spare a couple minutes to fill out my campaign’s 2026 Priorities Survey, Derek?** **[TAKE THE SURVEY](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/124938976/600177024/-963781499?refcode=MW_ATA_EM_SVY_PrioritiesRS_260207_T1_1_c&ms=MW_ATA_EM_SVY_PrioritiesRS_260207_T1_1_c&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNDAvMS84ODY1NCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI3NjdhN2FjNy02MDA0LWYxMTEtODMyZi0wMDBkM2ExZjBlNGMiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=M_VGVzgAGSwE2jVnd306KV_ZAKZojvFH75hEPvVVUso=&emci=3b6138c7-ac03-f111-832f-000d3a1f0e4c&emdi=767a7ac7-6004-f111-832f-000d3a1f0e4c&ceid=4568237)** So much has happened this year already, I know it feels overwhelming to keep track of the chaos.

Senate Republicans blocked bipartisan, House-passed legislation to extend ACA tax credits and lower costs for millions of Americans... the Trump administration continues to allow federal agents to terrorize our communities... Nothing is being done by Republicans to address the sky-high cost of living.

But I want to tell you that I’m keeping track of it all, Derek – and I need to know that we’re on the same page as we gear up to fight back in this critical election year.

[_**That’s why I’m asking you to spare two minutes to fill out my campaign’s 2026 Priorities Survey >>**_](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/124938977/600177028/-963781499?refcode=MW_ATA_EM_SVY_PrioritiesRS_260207_T1_1_c&ms=MW_ATA_EM_SVY_PrioritiesRS_260207_T1_1_c&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNDAvMS84ODY1NCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI3NjdhN2FjNy02MDA0LWYxMTEtODMyZi0wMDBkM2ExZjBlNGMiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=M_VGVzgAGSwE2jVnd306KV_ZAKZojvFH75hEPvVVUso=&emci=3b6138c7-ac03-f111-832f-000d3a1f0e4c&emdi=767a7ac7-6004-f111-832f-000d3a1f0e4c&ceid=4568237)

It wasn't easy telling the world I grew up dirt poor, I was raised by my Mamaw while my mother struggled with addiction.
It wasn't exactly the prep school/trust fund/summer-in-the-Hamptons upbringing that is commonplace in DC.
But I felt God called me to tell my story. Warts and all. I felt led to speak out because I believe millions of Americans share stories like mine. Stories of jobs being outsourced to China, addiction ravaging communities and killing our neighbors, and heeding the call of duty after the Towers fell on 9/11.
As your Vice President, I now stand in the breach for the left-behind, forgotten men and women who built this country, but were abandoned by the political class in DC.
I'll do everything in my power to make sure that never happens again. I'll fight every day for good folks like you.
I promise to always stand between you and the Democrat Machine that aims to obliterate everything that makes our country great.

This week, Early Voting kicked off in my race for U.S. Senate. So, as you read this, some Illinoisans are casting their ballots across the state and making decisions that will determine not just who represents them in Washington, but what kind of Senate we'll have for the next six years.
It's exciting to see democracy in action. But I'll be honest with you: it's also nerve-wracking. Because from this moment forward, every single day matters. Every conversation we have with voters, every ad we run, every volunteer we mobilize - it all translates directly into votes.
We're truly in the final stretch now. And I'm counting on your help to finish strong.
## **Why These Next Weeks Are Critical**
Let me explain what we're up against and why your support right now is so crucial:
**First, mobilizing our supporters and reaching undecided voters is a massive undertaking.** Right now, my team and I are traveling all over Illinois, meeting with voters across the state. We're powering an army of volunteers who are knocking on doors, making phone calls, and having conversations with their neighbors. We're broadcasting our message on TV to reach people who haven't made up their minds yet.
All of this costs money. Organizing infrastructure, volunteer materials, travel, media buys - it all adds up very quickly.
**Second, a Super PAC that has** _**already been caught misleading Illinoisans**_**is on the air with seven figures of ads supporting my opponent.** They're flooding the airwaves in this final stretch. We need to fight back immediately. We can't let their misleading ads go unanswered while voters are making their decisions.
**Third, if we fall short of our fundraising goals, we 'd have to pull back our efforts at the worst possible moment** - just as voters are making up their minds. Remember: every day from now on, thousands of votes across Illinois will be locked in. If we can't reach those voters before they cast their ballots, we've lost our chance to earn their support.
That's the reality of early voting. It's not a single Election Day anymore - it's weeks of voting, with decisions being made every single day.
## **What This Race Means**
I know I've been asking a lot of you throughout this campaign. But I want to make sure you understand what's at stake - not just for Illinois, but for the country.
This race will help determine whether we can flip the Senate and provide real oversight of the Trump administration. Whether we can restore the ACA tax credits that Republicans let expire. Whether we can hold ICE accountable for operating with impunity. Whether we can stop unconstitutional wars and demand that Congress exercise its constitutional war powers authority.
The MAGA-controlled Senate has completely abdicated its responsibility for oversight and accountability. They've rubber-stamped Trump's agenda, ignored abuses of power, and put corporate interests ahead of working families at every turn.
We can change that. But only if we win races like this one.
## **I 'm Counting on You**
So much is at stake. And I'm counting on you to dig a little deeper, to give what you can in this final stretch, so we can finish strong and win this race.
**[Will you rush $10, $25, or whatever you can afford today to help us mobilize the voters we need to win?](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/cc35edd6-8ac2-40ac-b47b-d2b751b11d8e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
[ RUSH A DONATION ->](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/cc35edd6-8ac2-40ac-b47b-d2b751b11d8e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Thank you for your support. Thank you for believing in this campaign. And thank you for being part of the movement to flip the Senate and fight for the future Illinois - and America - deserves.
Let's win this!
Raja Krishnamoorthi

"America's business is business," President Calvin Coolidge 30th President of United States
Looking at U.S. foreign policy in Latin America, I often examine how presidential doctrines evolve and intersect with contemporary crises. The administration of Donald J. Trump (2017-2021) provides a fascinating case study in this regard, particularly its approach to the Venezuelan crisis under Nicolas Maduro. At first glance, Trump's aggressive stance--marked by economic sanctions, diplomatic isolation, and recognition of opposition leader Juan Guaido as interim president in January 2019--might seem like a modern echo of the Monroe Doctrine, the 1823 policy that asserted U.S. hegemony in the Western Hemisphere and warned European powers against interference. However, upon closer scrutiny, Trump's Venezuela policy aligns more closely with the Wilsonian tradition of Woodrow Wilson (1913-1921), emphasizing moralistic interventionism, democracy promotion, and ideological crusades against autocracy. This shift represents a departure from the Monroe Doctrine's original pragmatic, isolationist roots, favoring instead a proactive, values-driven engagement that risks entangling the U.S. in internal affairs for the sake of global democratic ideals.
[Upgrade to paid](https://substack.com/redirect/2/eyJlIjoiaHR0cHM6Ly9oZWFydGxhbmRqb3VybmFsLnN1YnN0YWNrLmNvbS9zdWJzY3JpYmU_.gRZB0M4e9uTJjhb1B3zi0jIf15HdRwHY6LGVhfEy_nw?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget&utm_content=187205234)
To understand this comparison, we must first revisit the Monroe Doctrine's origins and evolution. Articulated by President James Monroe in his 1823 address to Congress, the doctrine was a defensive posture born of post-Napoleonic anxieties. The U.S., still a young republic, sought to prevent European recolonization of newly independent Latin American states, declaring the Americas closed to further European colonization or intervention. Secretary of State John Quincy Adams, the doctrine's intellectual architect, framed it as a policy of non-interference: the U.S. would not meddle in European affairs if Europe reciprocated in the Western Hemisphere. This was not idealism but realpolitik--protecting U.S. commercial interests and territorial security without committing to moral crusades. Over time, the doctrine morphed. Theodore Roosevelt's 1904 Corollary expanded it into an offensive tool, justifying U.S. interventions in Latin America to prevent instability that might invite European involvement, as seen in occupations of Cuba, Haiti, and the Dominican Republic. Yet even in its interventionist form, the Monroe Doctrine remained sphere-of-influence oriented: it prioritized stability and U.S. dominance over ideological transformation. Interventions were often paternalistic, aimed at "civilizing" neighbors through financial oversight or military occupation, but not necessarily democratizing them in a universal sense.

In contrast, Wilsonianism introduced a moral dimension to U.S. foreign policy, rooted in Progressive Era ideals of self-determination, collective security, and the spread of democracy. Woodrow Wilson, a former academic and idealist, viewed international relations through a lens of ethical imperatives. His Fourteen Points (1918) called for open diplomacy, free trade, and national self-determination, culminating in the League of Nations to prevent wars through multilateralism. Wilson intervened in Latin America--occupying Veracruz in 1914 and Haiti in 1915--not merely for stability but to foster democratic governance and combat "tyranny." His famous declaration that the world must be made "safe for democracy" during World War I exemplified this: U.S. power should remake nations in America's image, promoting liberal values as a path to peace. Critics, including realists like George Kennan, later derided Wilsonianism as messianic, leading to overreach in places like Vietnam or Iraq. Yet its legacy endures in post-Cold War interventions, from Bill Clinton's actions in the Balkans to George W. Bush's democracy promotion in the Middle East.

Turning to Trump's Venezuela policy, the parallels with Wilsonianism become evident in its ideological framing and proactive regime-change efforts. Venezuela's crisis escalated under Maduro, who succeeded Hugo Chavez in 2013. By 2017, hyperinflation, food shortages, and political repression had triggered mass protests and a refugee exodus affecting neighboring countries. Trump's response was multifaceted: imposing sanctions on Venezuelan oil (PDVSA) in 2019, freezing assets, and barring U.S. firms from dealing with Maduro's regime. More dramatically, the U.S. recognized Guaido, the National Assembly president, as legitimate leader, rallying over 50 nations to do the same. This was not just economic pressure but a direct challenge to Maduro's sovereignty, justified in moral terms. Trump and officials like Secretary of State Mike Pompeo repeatedly invoked human rights abuses, electoral fraud, and the need to restore "democracy and freedom" in Venezuela. In a 2019 speech to the Venezuelan American community, Trump declared, "The days of socialism and communism are numbered not only in Venezuela, but in Nicaragua and Cuba as well," echoing Wilson's anti-autocratic rhetoric.

This approach diverges from the Monroe Doctrine in key ways. Traditionally, Monroe's policy focused on external threats: preventing foreign powers from gaining footholds in the Americas. In Venezuela, external actors like Russia, China, and Iran indeed supported Maduro--Russia with military advisors and debt relief, China with loans, and Iran with oil shipments. A pure Monroeist might have emphasized countering these influences to maintain U.S. hemispheric primacy, perhaps through quiet diplomacy or targeted actions against foreign assets. Instead, Trump's policy prioritized internal transformation: ousting Maduro to install a democratic government. This mirrors Wilson's interventions, where the goal was not just repelling outsiders but engineering regime change for ideological purity. For instance, Wilson's occupation of Haiti aimed to impose constitutional reforms and elections, much like Trump's support for Guaido's "interim government" and calls for free elections. Moreover, Trump's multilateralism--coordinating with the Lima Group and Organization of American States (OAS)--evokes Wilson's League of Nations vision, where collective action enforces democratic norms.

Critics might argue that Trump's real motivations were Monroeist: protecting U.S. energy interests (Venezuela holds vast oil reserves) and curbing migration flows. Sanctions did aim to starve Maduro of revenue, potentially benefiting U.S. oil producers amid the shale boom. The refugee crisis, displacing over 5 million Venezuelans by 2020, strained Colombia and Brazil, indirectly affecting U.S. borders. Yet these pragmatic elements were subordinated to a Wilsonian narrative. Unlike Monroe's non-ideological stance, Trump's rhetoric framed the conflict as a moral battle against "socialist tyranny." Pompeo's 2019 tour of Latin America warned of "malign" influences but tied them to the broader fight for "liberty." Even the failed 2020 "Operation Gideon"--a botched mercenary incursion allegedly tacitly supported by U.S. elements--recalls Wilson's covert meddling in Mexico during the 1910s, where ideological zeal overrode caution.
Furthermore, Trump's policy lacked the Monroe Doctrine's restraint on entanglement. Monroe and Adams advocated "non-interference" in internal politics unless vital interests were at stake. Roosevelt's Corollary intervened only when "chronic wrongdoing" invited European action. In Venezuela, no immediate European recolonization loomed; the threats were from non-Western powers, but Trump's response went beyond containment to active promotion of self-determination. Guaido's recognition effectively declared Maduro's 2018 election illegitimate, intervening in Venezuela's domestic legitimacy--a Wilsonian hallmark. Wilson similarly refused to recognize Mexican dictator Victoriano Huerta in 1913, insisting on "constitutional" rule. Both cases reflect a belief that U.S. power should arbitrate foreign governance based on democratic standards, risking escalation. Trump's threats of military options ("all options are on the table") amplified this, though no invasion occurred, unlike Wilson's Veracruz landing.

The Wilsonian tilt also explains the policy's limitations and backlash. Like Wilson's idealism, Trump's approach overestimated U.S. leverage. Sanctions crippled Venezuela's economy, reducing GDP by over 70% since 2013, but Maduro endured through repression and foreign alliances. Guaido's momentum faded by 2021, with Maduro consolidating power. This mirrors Wilson's post-World War I failures: the Senate rejected the League, and self-determination ideals faltered in practice. In Latin America, Trump's policy alienated left-leaning governments wary of U.S. interventionism, reviving memories of Cold War-era overthrows like Guatemala (1954) or Chile (1973). A more Monroeist strategy--focusing on bilateral deals to isolate foreign influences without regime change--might have been less divisive.

While elements of the Monroe Doctrine persist in Trump's "run" Venezuela policy--such as countering external powers--the overriding emphasis on democracy promotion, moral rhetoric, and internal transformation marks it as profoundly Wilsonian. This blend reflects a broader trend in U.S. foreign policy: the tension between realist spheres of influence and idealist global missions.

As historian Walter Russell Mead notes, Wilsonianism appeals to American exceptionalism, viewing the U.S. as a beacon of liberty. Trump, often labeled an isolationist, ironically embraced this in Venezuela, perhaps influenced by neoconservative advisors like John Bolton. The result was a policy that, while failing to dislodge Maduro, underscored Wilsonianism's enduring allure and perils. In an era of great-power competition, future administrations might weigh whether such ideological interventions serve U.S. interests or merely perpetuate cycles of resentment in the Americas.

* * *
* * *
Remember when Hollywood couldn't stop draping itself in Ukrainian flags like it was the new designer accessory of 2022? Oscars, Grammys, Golden Globes--every red carpet looked like a walking Ukrainian embassy. Benedict Cumberbatch rocking a pocket square in blue and yellow, Jamie Lee Curtis turning a ribbon into jewelry, Jason Momoa channeling Aquaman solidarity. They were "standing with Ukraine," virtue-signaling so hard you could hear the Zelenskyy applause from Kyiv. Performative? Sure. But at least it was consistent for a hot minute.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/27208690-8d3f-4d1e-a8e6-40161fe7181e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Fast-forward to 2025, and the love affair was still flickering. At the Oscars in March--right after President Trump's Oval Office dust-up with Zelenskyy, where the Ukrainian leader showed up in his signature war-time formalwear (black polo with trident crest and fatigue pants, like he was auditioning for a Netflix war flick)--Daryl Hannah couldn't resist going off-script. Presenting Best Film Editing, she flashed a victory sign and belted out "Slava Ukraini!" to roaring applause. "Glory to Ukraine," she declared, because nothing says courage like a 64-year-old actress yelling battle cries from a Dolby Theatre stage amid fresh White House drama. Trump quipped, "Oh look, you're all dressed up," dripping with sarcasm--Zelenskyy looked like he'd rolled out of a bunker, not suited for diplomacy.
"Conclave" writer Peter Straughan pinned a Ukrainian flag brooch to his tux and told Variety, "Just to say, let's not turn our backs on Ukraine." The "Porcelain War" doc team (about Ukrainian artists-turned-fighters) sported the same pins. Even Adam Sandler's sweatshirt got memed as a Zelenskyy nod. Hollywood was still fawning over the cause, still pinning hopes (and actual pins) on the war effort, still pretending their lapel statements would end Putin's aggression.
Then came 2026. Poof. Gone.
The Ukraine flags vanished as fast as the left's outrage under Biden--when they cheered endless billions flowing to Kyiv while borders bled and high-profile crimes by released criminal aliens made headlines. Back then, media coverage was wall-to-wall: Ukraine as the moral crusade of the decade, Hollywood draping itself in blue-and-yellow like it was saving the world one ribbon at a time. Biden's administration poured in aid without end, and the left/media ate it up--no fatigue, no questions about the grinding stalemate or the generational wipeout.
But flip the script to domestic enforcement: Suddenly, the same crowd--Billie Eilish, Bad Bunny, Justin and Hailey Bieber, Joni Mitchell, Kehlani--trades flags for "ICE Out" pins and "F--- ICE" speeches at the Grammys, honoring victims of federal actions while glossing over the Biden-era chaos that left **662,566 noncitizens with criminal histories** on ICE's national docket as of mid- 2024 including **435,719 convicted criminals** and **226,847 with pending charges.** Encounters topped **10.8 million nationwide since FY2021,** fueling tragedies like the rape and murder of Laken Riley (by an illegal alien) and the sexual assault and killing of 12-year-old Jocelyn Nungaray (by two illegal aliens). The unauthorized population peaked at **13.7 -14 million** by mid-2023 (per Pew and MPI estimates), a record high after years of lax policies.
Worse? Biden's open borders imported the murderous Tren de Aragua (TDA) Venezuelan gang--now tied to 100+ ongoing investigations in the United States, including cases involving murders, rapes, assaults, and trafficking in states like New York, Illinois, Florida, Texas, and Colorado. Under Biden, TDA exploited the migrant surge to infiltrate, terrorizing communities and preying on Americans and migrants alike. Families shattered, communities destabilized--real suffering the left ignores while pinning anti-ICE badges.
Now? FBI Director Kash Patel's 2025 stats deliver the slap: Violent crime arrests surged 200% overall (67,000 total), with 490% jumps in takedowns of murderers, rapists, and child molesters; homicides dropped 21% in 35 major cities (922 fewer deaths), aggravated assaults and robberies plummeted. ICE nabbed 132,000+ in the first half (70% with criminal records), deportations quadrupled, and hundreds of TDA members booted using the Alien Enemies Act. Trump's fixes are cleaning up Biden's mess, prioritizing American safety over performative pity.
The numbers sting harder on Ukraine: Zelenskyy admits 55,000 Ukrainian soldiers dead; Russian losses 275,000-325,000 killed; total casualties nearing 1.8 million (on pace for 2 million by spring, per CSIS). U.S. taxpayers? $175-187 billion appropriated since 2022 ($128-130 billion direct to Kyiv) for a stalemate grinding on.
Hollywood's response? Pins defending the system that let horrors happen, speeches shielding the same crowd jacking violent stats. This isn't evolution; it's expiration. Hollywood's solidarity has a sell-by date shorter than milk in July. They fawned over Zelenskyy when it was fashionable, pinned flags when the cameras loved it, then swapped them for "ICE Out" buttons the second the domestic outrage cycle spun up.
The audience knows performative activism when they see it. The left's lapel politics flip like a bad Netflix series--big emotions, short attention span. If they can drop Ukraine this fast after years of chest-thumping, what's next? Another pin for the next viral crisis?
Until then, keep your eyes on those red carpets. The next virtue signal is always just one tragedy--or one trending cause--away.

| | Hi Peter, it’s Rep. Zoe Lofgren.

Last week, House and Senate Republicans re-introduced the SAVE Act, or the “Safeguard American Voter Eligibility Act.” Let me be clear: **This is another blatant attempt at voter suppression by Republicans. ** The SAVE Act promises to require “documentary proof of U.S. citizenship to register to vote in federal elections.” But let’s take a look at what it actually does: ❌ It requires a passport or birth certificate to vote, disenfranchising huge blocks of eligible voters including the _21 million Americans_ who lack access to these registration documents (**_that’s_********_over 9% of voting age citizens!_**). ❌ It threatens online voter registration AND vote-by-mail, making it significantly harder for the millions of Americans who rely on these systems to make their vote count. ❌ And it requires regular voter roll purges, which historically block eligible Americans from voting by incorrectly wiping them from the records. Peter, I believe that we should make it easier for Americans to participate in our democracy, not put up ridiculous hurdles to disenfranchise our constituents. That’s why I voted against this bill the last time it was introduced, and I’ll continue to fight against it and push for new legislation that expands voting rights and protections instead of erasing them. **[If you’re with me and want to see an end to these far-right attacks on our democracy, then please donate to my campaign today to re-elect me and more Democrats who will stand up for your rights.](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/124941360/600184844/-1463031945?amount=25&refcode=EM_ALL_ZOL_FR_1_2026-02-07_VTR_SVA_ES-41311&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMDMvMS82OTYwNiIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIzMWVkMzkwMS03NjA0LWYxMTEtODMyZi0wMDBkM2ExZjBlNGMiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=osXIEm0MkMoryhmTgPgVNegXD2WiaaBRcA2mnyIYTII=)**

Every year, EMILYs List recognizes a woman currently serving in a state or local office with our **Gabrielle Giffords Rising Star Award**. clean_body: We need you! Time to add your voice >> | You know who the emerging leaders are in your community, Peter, and we want to hear about them! | Peter, As you know, leaders come from every place and every background imaginable. Is there a rising star in your community? Now is your chance to celebrate her on a national level! Every year, EMILYs List recognizes a woman currently serving in a state or local office with our Gabrielle Giffords Rising Star Award. This award highlights a leader with a promising career in public service, and honors her for showing the same dedication, determination, and commitment as our award's namesake. The recipient of the 2026 Rising Star Award will not only be honored at our annual We Are EMILY event this spring, but will also know that the millions-strong EMILYs List community sees her work and has her back! Past recipients have included Virginia Delegate Adele McClure , Harris County Judge Lina Hidalgo , and former state representative and now U.S. Rep. Emilia Sykes (OH-13). These women have made a huge difference in their cities, states, and our country. We are so excited to find and honor our next rising star, but first, we need your help to find her! clean_body: What you’re seeing happen in Minnesota right now is a preview of what's to come if Democrats flip the Senate in November. | Peter, As a Republican political candidate running to represent Minnesota in the U.S. Senate, here is what I can tell you from being here during one of the most tumultuous times in recent memory. 1. Democrats believe that they have a reasonably straightforward path to any higher office that they want, simply because our state hasn’t voted for a Republican candidate on the presidential level since 1976 2. The mayor of Minneapolis and Governor Walz like to openly vilify Republicans, believing their supporters would never toss them to the curb simply because they are playing the role of attack dog. The mayor is probably even more of a left-wing ideologue than the governor. 3. They hate President Trump and everything he stands for - that’s why they are not cooperating with ICE in any way, shape, or form. Now, the mayor, the governor, and my opponent in this Senate race, Lieutenant Governor Peggy Flanagan, are digging in even further, comparing FEDERAL ICE agents to neighbors flooding the city that don’t share the same values as the original inhabitants. But what about the millions of illegal immigrants who flooded our country that don’t share ANY of our values? Democrats in Minnesota are showing the entire country what exactly will happen if they retake the Senate in November or the White House in 2028. They tolerate flash mobs, violent protests, and they don’t say anything when crazed lunatics storm places of worship, all to prove a point. But what do you expect from a lieutenant governor who makes a mockery out of herself by cosplaying as a muslim? Rather than hand over convicted and suspected criminals to federal authorities, the mayor of Minneapolis and Governor Tim Walz released them into Minnesota communities. Somalian immigrants are storming the state capital building. As a former Navy SEAL, I have been trained to rout out corruption, quell violent uprisings, and, most importantly, lead a team with honor. This is a no-fail mission, and Navy SEALS win races. It’s a proven fact. SEALS are entrusted with our nation’s most important, covert missions that have national security implications which impact every single American - and I can tell you that as a candidate for political office, I’m ready for this no-fail mission and my opponents are not. clean_body: Peter, It's Jen Kiggans and Derrick Van Orden, and we're grateful you opened this, but will be even more grateful if you can read it all the way through. The Democrats have named their top targets for 2026, and we're not surprised to see our names at the top of the list. You see, we both won seats that were previously held by Democrats in 2022. Then, we both PROTECTED our seats in 2024 after they dumped MILLIONS into our districts to try and beat us. The Democrats are foaming at the mouth to take these seats back from us. But it's not going to be easy, and we'll tell you why...| | ---|--- We're both Navy Vets who have looked the enemy in the eye before. We won't be intimidated by a bunch of woke wahoos who think men should be allowed in women's locker rooms or think we should let illegal immigrants vote in our elections. We know that they're going to smear our records, attack us in the press, and air lying attack ads- because that's exactly what they did last year, too! But it didn't work then, and it won't work now. We're building the strongest teams we can, and filling our war chests so that when the fight knocks on our front door in 2026, we're ready. We need you to help us make sure that we have the resources we'll need to protect our seats. Can we count on you? We won't forget what you've done to help us today. Thank you, Jen Kiggans (VA-02) Derrick Van Orden (WI-03) I would not be where I am today without the help of my incredible and faithful supporters like you.
